Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the ICFR framework, the COSO-mapped control matrix and management's Item 308(a) assessment; the SOX Program Manager runs the annual scoping and testing calendar and reports deficiencies to the CFO

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - SOX 404(a) and 404(b) (15 U.S.C. 7262), Reg S-K Item 308(a)/(b) (17 CFR 229.308), Rule 13a-15(c) and the Rule 12b-2 accelerated-filer definition that drives whether the 404(b) attestation applies, re-read on eCFR at annual scoping and dated in the scoping memo

In-scope processes.value: Financial close and consolidation, premium and unearned premium accounting, claims and loss reserves to ledger, investment accounting, ceded reinsurance accounting, treasury, payroll and income tax - every process feeding a 10-K or 10-Q line above the scoping materiality threshold, plus ITGCs over the GL and the policy and claims subledger feeds

In-scope systems.value: GL and consolidation, BlackLine close and reconciliations, Guidewire PolicyCenter and ClaimCenter subledger feeds and the actuarial reserving platform sit inside the ICFR boundary; the control matrix and all test evidence live in AuditBoard

Compliance procedure documented.value: SOX Program Manual - annual scoping memo, COSO 2013 seventeen-principle mapping, control matrix maintenance rules, walkthrough and testing standards, IPE validation, deficiency evaluation and aggregation, and the drafting of management's Item 308(a) report

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and the CFO and ratified by the Audit Committee at its first-quarter meeting; re-approved on any change of filer status, ERP or policy-admin implementation, or acquisition that adds an in-scope entity

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Management's Item 308(a) assessment and the auditor's Item 308(b) attestation must be final before the 10-K filing date (60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer, 75 for accelerated, 90 for non-accelerated); material ICFR changes are disclosed each quarter in Part I Item 4 of the 10-Q

Deadline reminders configured.value: SOX calendar milestones with T-30/T-10/T-2 alerts: scoping memo signed by 31 May, interim testing complete by 30 September, roll-forward complete by 31 January, deficiency aggregation memo delivered 10 business days before the 10-K filing date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Control matrix versions, walkthrough memos, test scripts and samples, IPE validation, deficiency logs, remediation retests and the signed 308(a) assessment retained 7 years under the 18 U.S.C. 1520 audit-record rule in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every failed control attribute is logged as a deficiency rated control deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness, with the compensating control, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CAE validates remediation retesting before any deficiency is closed; a material weakness closes only after a full-period retest and a minuted Audit Committee acknowledgement

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All key controls in the approved annual SOX scope across in-scope entities covering the target percentages of consolidated revenue, total assets and pre-tax income, plus all ITGCs for access, change and operations over the GL, close tool, policy admin, claims and reserving systems

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Attribute sampling with zero-deviation acceptance: 25 items for daily controls, 15 for weekly, 5 for monthly, 2 for quarterly, 1 for annual; one deviation triggers root cause and a single double sample; an unremediated material weakness makes the Item 308(a) conclusion not effective

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: ICFR operates continuously, so controls are tested at interim in Q2 and Q3 and rolled forward through year end, with the effectiveness conclusion reached as of the fiscal year end balance sheet date

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit tests only controls it does not perform; no tester may test a control in a process they operate, supervise or account for

Evidence location for test results.value: AuditBoard SOX workspace holding the matrix, walkthroughs, test scripts, samples, IPE support and exceptions, with the locked year-end binder copied to the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The SOX binder - scoping memo, control matrix, walkthrough memos, test results, deficiency evaluation, the 308(a) assessment and the auditor's 308(b) opinion - producible to an SEC comment letter or a PCAOB inspection request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: General Counsel owns SEC comment-letter responses on Item 9A and Item 308; the CFO and the Audit Committee chair clear any material-weakness disclosure or Item 4.02 non-reliance conclusion before it is filed on EDGAR

checklist.step: Set the annual ICFR scope from the filed financial statements
actions: Pull the prior-year 10-K trial balance by legal entity and account from the GL reporting tree and load it into the scoping workbook.
Set planning materiality with the CFO - commonly 5% of pre-tax income or 0.5% of total assets for an insurer - then set the individual account threshold at one third of that figure.
Mark every account above threshold plus loss reserves, reinsurance recoverables and deferred acquisition costs regardless of size because of their estimation risk.
Confirm entity coverage reaches the target percentage of consolidated revenue, assets and pre-tax income and list every entity excluded with the reason.
Write the scoping memo, have the Controller sign it, and file it as the first tab of the AuditBoard SOX workspace.
checklist.done: a signed scoping memo names the in-scope entities, accounts and coverage percentages with the materiality basis shown.

checklist.step: Confirm filer status and whether the 404(b) auditor attestation is required
actions: Compute worldwide public float as of the last business day of the most recently completed second fiscal quarter using the closing price and the non-affiliate share count from the transfer agent.

Apply Rule 12b-2: large accelerated at 700 million or more, accelerated at 75 million or more, and test the smaller reporting company revenue test under 100 million that exempts an issuer from 404(b).
Record the resulting cover-page check boxes for the 10-K and confirm them with the Corporate Secretary who owns the cover page.
Notify the Controller and the engagement partner in writing whether an Item 308(b) attestation is in scope this year.
checklist.done: filer status is computed from float and revenue, documented, and the 404(b) applicability decision is communicated in writing.

checklist.step: Refresh the process, risk and control matrix for every in-scope process
actions: Open each in-scope process in the AuditBoard control matrix and re-confirm with the process owner the risks of material misstatement by assertion - existence, completeness, valuation, rights and obligations, presentation.
For each control record the control id, description, owner, frequency, preventive or detective, manual or automated, key or non-key, the assertions covered and the systems and reports relied on.
Retire controls for processes that no longer exist and add controls for new products, new reinsurance treaties or systems implemented during the year.
Flag every control that relies on a system-generated report so it enters the IPE testing queue.
Have each process owner electronically attest to their section of the matrix in AuditBoard.
checklist.done: every in-scope process has an owner-attested matrix with no control lacking an assertion, a frequency and an evidence source.

checklist.step: Map the control set to the COSO 2013 framework and find the gaps
actions: Map each key control to one or more of the seventeen COSO 2013 principles across the five components and record the mapping on the control record.
List any principle with no supporting control - typically Principle 8 fraud risk or Principle 16 ongoing evaluations - and raise it as a design gap with an owner.
Run the annual fraud risk assessment workshop with the Controller, the Chief Audit Executive and Legal and map each identified scheme to a mitigating control.
Document the conclusion that all five components are present and functioning, because Item 308(a) requires the framework used to be identified and applied in full.
checklist.done: each COSO principle is supported by at least one mapped control or has a logged design gap with a remediation owner.

checklist.step: Walk through each significant process end to end with the process owner
actions: Book a walkthrough with the process owner and follow one live transaction from initiation to its appearance in the GL and in the disclosure.
At each control point ask who performs it, what they compare, what threshold triggers follow-up, what they do when it fails and where the evidence lands.
Capture screenshots of the system steps - the approval screen, the BlackLine reconciliation certification, the journal posting - and the source documents used.
Write the walkthrough memo with a process flow, the control points and a design-effectiveness conclusion, and have the process owner countersign it.
Update the matrix the same day where the walkthrough contradicts the documented control.
checklist.done: a countersigned walkthrough memo with a flow, control points and a design-effectiveness conclusion exists for each significant process.

checklist.step: Scope and test the IT general controls over in-scope systems
actions: List the in-scope layers - application, database, operating system - for the GL, close tool, policy admin, claims and reserving platforms.
Test access provisioning by pulling all joiners in the period from the IAM platform and matching each to an approved access request and a role that matches the job.
Test the quarterly user access review: confirm every reviewer certified in SailPoint, that revocations were actioned within the SLA, and re-check privileged and generic accounts.
Test change management by pulling all production changes from the CI/CD pipeline and matching each to an approved ticket, evidence of testing and separation between developer and deployer.
Test batch job monitoring and backup or restore for the GL interfaces and record the failure follow-up evidence.
Hand exceptions to the SOX Program Manager naming the automated and report-dependent controls affected.
checklist.done: each ITGC domain is tested at every in-scope layer and exceptions are handed over with their downstream control impact identified.

checklist.step: Validate the completeness and accuracy of every report used in a key control
actions: For each IPE report obtain from the report developer the source system, the report or query definition, the parameters and the filters applied.
Re-run the report with the same parameters and agree the record count and a key total back to the source system or the GL balance.
Where the report is a spreadsheet, test formula integrity, hidden rows and manual override cells and confirm the file sits in a controlled, access-restricted location.
Record the parameters screenshot, the reconciliation and the conclusion for each report in the workpaper.
checklist.done: every report a key control relies on has a documented completeness and accuracy conclusion with a reconciliation to source.

checklist.step: Test the precision of management review controls over estimates
actions: For each management review control over loss reserves, DAC, investment impairments and reinsurance recoverables, obtain the review package the reviewer actually used.
Document the precision - the specific threshold, expectation or variance percentage the reviewer compared against - not merely that they signed.
Select instances where an outlier appeared and trace the reviewer's question, the preparer's answer and the resulting adjustment or documented acceptance.
Log a design deficiency where the review is only a sign-off with no stated threshold and no evidence of investigation.
checklist.done: each management review control has a documented precision threshold and evidence of at least one investigated outlier.

checklist.step: Agree the testing approach and auditor reliance before interim testing
actions: Send the scoping memo, control matrix and test plan to the engagement partner and hold the planning meeting before interim testing starts.
Agree which controls the auditor will rely on management's testing for and the reperformance percentage the auditor will apply.
Agree the evidence format and the delivery dates so workpapers are not reworked in January.
Record the reliance list and every control the auditor will test directly, and share it with the Audit Committee chair in the pre-meeting.
checklist.done: a written reliance agreement with the engagement team lists controls, testing owner and evidence delivery dates.

checklist.step: Execute interim testing and record results control by control
actions: Draw each sample from the full population of control occurrences for the interim period using the frequency-based sample sizes in the plan, and record the population source and selection method.
Test each sampled item against the written attributes and record pass or fail per attribute with the evidence attached to the sample line in AuditBoard.
Obtain the process owner's written explanation for every deviation before concluding, and expand the sample only where the plan permits.
Set each control's interim conclusion in AuditBoard and route failed controls straight into the deficiency log.
checklist.done: every in-scope key control has an interim conclusion supported by attached, attribute-level evidence.

checklist.step: Roll interim conclusions forward to the fiscal year end
actions: For each control tested at interim ask the process owner in writing whether the control, its performer or its system changed in the roll-forward period.
Test additional occurrences from the roll-forward period - typically 2 to 5 items depending on frequency - for every key control.
Re-test in full any control whose owner, system or design changed after interim testing.
Document the roll-forward conclusion so the effectiveness statement genuinely speaks as of the balance sheet date.
checklist.done: each control has roll-forward evidence and a conclusion stated as of fiscal year end, with changed controls fully retested.

checklist.step: Evaluate and aggregate deficiencies to a severity conclusion
actions: For each deficiency compute the potential magnitude as the gross exposure of the affected account or transaction stream and assess the likelihood a misstatement would not be prevented or detected.
Classify as control deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness and record the compensating controls considered and why they do or do not mitigate.
Aggregate deficiencies affecting the same account or assertion, because individually minor items combine into a material weakness.

Present the deficiency evaluation memo to the Controller, the CFO and the engagement partner at least 10 business days before the 10-K filing date and resolve any classification disagreement in writing.
checklist.done: every deficiency carries a magnitude, a likelihood and a severity rating, aggregated by account and agreed with the external auditor.

checklist.step: Drive remediation and retest before the assessment date
actions: Assign each open deficiency an owner, a remediation action and a target date that leaves enough operating occurrences to retest before year end.
Confirm the remediated control has operated for a sufficient period - a monthly control needs at least three post-remediation occurrences - before retesting.
Retest with a fresh sample drawn only from the post-remediation period and never reuse the original failed items.
Close the deficiency in AuditBoard only on a clean retest and carry anything still open into the Audit Committee pack.
checklist.done: each remediated deficiency has a clean post-remediation retest and open items are reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Draft management's Item 308(a) report and the support for the 302 certifications
actions: Draft the Item 9A text: management's responsibility statement, the framework identified as COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013), the assessment as of fiscal year end and the effectiveness conclusion.
Attach the sub-certification pack - signed representations from each process and entity controller confirming no undisclosed deficiencies, fraud or unrecorded items.
Assemble the Rule 13a-14 certification support binder for the CEO and CFO cross-referencing each numbered paragraph of the 302 certification to its evidence.
Disclose in Item 9A any material change in ICFR during the fourth quarter and describe any material weakness with its remediation plan.
Route the draft to General Counsel and the Disclosure Committee for review before typesetting.
checklist.done: a Disclosure Committee reviewed Item 9A draft exists with sub-certifications and a paragraph-level 302 support binder.

checklist.step: Obtain the auditor's Item 308(b) attestation and file the annual report
actions: Deliver the final management assessment and the complete SOX binder to the engagement partner and hold the clearance meeting with the Audit Committee.
Obtain the signed auditor opinion on ICFR effectiveness and confirm the framework named and the as-of date match management's report exactly.
Confirm the opinion appears in Item 8 or Item 9A as Item 308(b) requires, and that the auditor consent and the PCAOB firm identifier are present.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that the Audit Committee approved the filing and that the certifications are executed as Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 and furnished as 32.1 and 32.2.
Release the 10-K on EDGAR before the filer-status deadline and archive the accepted filing and the EDGAR acceptance message in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: the 10-K carries a signed auditor ICFR opinion matching management's framework and as-of date and is accepted on EDGAR before the deadline.

testing.step: Rebuild the in-scope control population independently of the SOX team
actions: Export the full key-control list from AuditBoard with process, entity, frequency, assertions and tester as of the year-end lock date.
Independently re-derive the account scope from the year-end trial balance using the documented materiality threshold and compare it to the scoping memo.
List every account above threshold with no mapped key control and every in-scope entity excluded from testing.
Reconcile the control count to the prior year and obtain a written explanation for every control added, retired or downgraded from key to non-key.
testing.done: the independently rebuilt scope reconciles to the scoping memo with every difference explained in writing.

testing.step: Reconcile the control matrix to the general ledger and the filed disclosures
actions: Agree the trial balance used for scoping to the consolidated balance sheet and income statement filed in the 10-K, line by line.
Trace each significant disclosure - the loss reserve roll-forward, reinsurance, the fair value hierarchy, segments - to a control covering its preparation and review.
Flag any filed disclosure with no owning control as a scope gap, because Item 308(a) covers disclosure preparation and not only the primary statements.
Record the reconciliation and the gap list in the workpaper with the 10-K page references.
testing.done: the scoping trial balance agrees to the filed statements and every significant disclosure maps to a named control.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of tested controls for reperformance
actions: Take 100% of controls over loss reserves, reinsurance recoverables and investment valuation, plus every control with a prior-year deficiency.
Draw 30 further controls at random with a recorded seed from the remaining key-control population, stratified across entity and process.
Record the population size, the seed, the selection date and the stratification so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Confirm no sampled control was tested or owned by the reviewer performing this test.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed, covers all estimate-heavy and prior-deficiency controls and is free of self-review.

testing.step: Reperform testing on the sampled controls without reading the original conclusion
actions: Draw a fresh sample of occurrences for each sampled control from the same population and test the written attributes before opening the original workpaper.
For automated controls re-execute the configuration test in the source system - for example post a journal breaching the tolerance and confirm the block fires.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded one; a difference in conclusion, in sample size or in the attributes tested is an exception.
Attach your independent evidence to the workpaper alongside the original test line.
testing.done: each sampled control carries an independent reperformance conclusion and any divergence from the original is logged.

testing.step: Verify sample sizes, populations and IPE support behind the original testing
actions: Compare the sample size used for each sampled control to the frequency table in the approved test plan and flag under-sampling.
Obtain the population extract used for selection and re-run the query yourself to confirm it covered the full period rather than only the interim months.
Confirm the IPE reports supporting the sampled controls have a documented completeness and accuracy conclusion with a reconciliation to source.
Treat a control tested from an incomplete population as untested rather than as a documentation point.
testing.done: sample sizes match the plan, populations are re-derived as complete and every relied-on report has IPE support.

testing.step: Trace ITGC conclusions to the automated controls that depend on them
actions: Pull the ITGC exception list and map each exception to the application controls and reports sitting on that layer.
For each access or change-management exception decide and document whether the dependent automated control can still be relied on or must be tested manually for the affected period.
Re-pull the year-end privileged access list from SailPoint and confirm no developer holds production posting rights in the GL.
Log the failure to reassess a dependent control after an ITGC exception as a testing-methodology exception.
testing.done: every ITGC exception is traced to its dependent controls with a documented reliance or fallback decision.

testing.step: Recompute the deficiency severity and aggregation maths
actions: Recompute the potential magnitude of each deficiency against the gross exposure of the affected account rather than the misstatement actually found.
Re-aggregate deficiencies by account and by assertion and test whether any combination reaches the material weakness threshold.
Compare each classification to the external auditor's own severity assessment and document any disagreement and its resolution.
Recompute whether remediated controls operated for enough post-remediation occurrences before retest, since a short operating window does not support closure.
testing.done: severity and aggregation are independently recomputed, agree with the auditor, and closure timing is validated.

testing.step: Verify the 308(a) report, the 308(b) opinion and the certifications as filed
actions: Open the filed 10-K on EDGAR and read Item 9A against the Item 308(a) elements - responsibility statement, framework named, as-of date and effectiveness conclusion.
Confirm the auditor's ICFR opinion is present where 404(b) applies and that its framework reference and as-of date match management's report word for word.
Confirm Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 carry the Rule 13a-14 certification text unaltered and that 32.1 and 32.2 are furnished, all signed by the serving CEO and CFO.
Recompute the filing deadline from fiscal year end using the filer status on the cover page and compare it to the EDGAR acceptance timestamp.
testing.done: the filed Item 9A, auditor opinion and certifications are complete and consistent and the filing beat the recomputed deadline.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the control id, the process, what failed and the potential financial statement impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list - scope omission, insufficient sample, unvalidated IPE, imprecise review control, ITGC dependency ignored, late remediation - and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next interim testing cycle and escalate immediately to the CFO and General Counsel anything that would change the filed Item 9A conclusion.
Carry every open issue into next year's test plan as a mandatory retest line.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the reperformance exception rate and compare it to the zero-deviation acceptance criterion in the test plan.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or not effective - with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who tested none of the sampled controls and owns none of them, sign the workpaper.
Present the results, open deficiencies and any disagreement with the external auditor to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception rate and is reported to the Audit Committee and archived.

checklist.step: Build the annual key-control test plan and get it approved
actions: Export the key-control population from AuditBoard and rank each control by inherent risk, prior-year exceptions, manual versus automated and estimate sensitivity.
Set testing timing per control - interim, roll-forward or year-end only - and the sample size drawn from the frequency table.
Add the entity-level governance controls explicitly: code-of-ethics adoption and availability, waiver approval and 8-K reporting, Regulation FD gatekeeping and the say-on-pay vote-cycle control.
Present the plan and the hours budget to the Audit Committee at the first-quarter meeting and record the approval in the minutes.
checklist.done: an Audit Committee approved plan lists every control with its timing, sample size and tester, including the governance entity-level controls.

checklist.step: Write testable attributes for the code-of-ethics control
actions: Read Item 406(b) and list the elements the code must address: honest and ethical conduct, handling of conflicts of interest, full fair accurate and timely disclosure in SEC filings, compliance with law, prompt internal reporting of violations and accountability for adherence.
Write one test attribute per element plus attributes confirming coverage of the principal executive officer, principal financial officer and principal accounting officer or controller.

Add an availability attribute matching the Item 406(c) option actually elected - filed as an exhibit, posted on the investor website with the URL given in the 10-K, or provided free on request with that undertaking disclosed.
Have General Counsel confirm the attribute set matches the disclosure the company actually makes in 10-K Part III and the proxy.
checklist.done: the code-of-ethics control has one attribute per Item 406 element plus an availability attribute matching the elected disclosure method.

checklist.step: Test that the published code still covers the required officers and content
actions: Download the code of ethics from the investor relations website and record the URL and the capture date.
Confirm the posted version matches the board-approved version in the board portal by comparing version number and approval date to the minutes.
Test each Item 406 content attribute against the actual text and cite the section number where each element is satisfied.
Open the filed 10-K Part III and confirm the disclosure names the code, identifies the officers covered and gives the exact URL or exhibit number.
Log any drift between the posted, board-approved and disclosed versions as an exception.
checklist.done: the posted, board-approved and 10-K-disclosed versions are identical and every Item 406 element is cited to a section of the code.

checklist.step: Test the waiver pipeline end to end for the year
actions: Extract every conflict-of-interest disclosure, related-party approval and code exception raised in the ethics case system for the year, not only those already labelled waiver.
For each, decide with General Counsel whether it is an implicit or explicit waiver for an executive officer or director as Item 406(d) defines those terms.
For every qualifying waiver confirm board or board-committee approval is minuted and that a Form 8-K Item 5.05 was filed, or the website posting made, within 4 business days of the approval date.
Compute and record on the test line the elapsed business days from approval to disclosure for each waiver.
Escalate any waiver with no disclosure to General Counsel the same day for a late-filing assessment.
checklist.done: every code exception is classified and each qualifying waiver has minuted approval and disclosure within 4 business days with the day count recorded.

checklist.step: Test the Regulation FD selective-disclosure control
actions: Pull the year's investor interaction log - earnings calls, conferences, one-on-one meetings, analyst calls, non-deal roadshows - with date, attendees and materials used.
Confirm every deck or script used was pre-cleared by the Disclosure Committee and traced to already-public information or furnished on Form 8-K Item 7.01.
For each logged inadvertent disclosure confirm public dissemination happened promptly - within 24 hours or before the opening of the next NYSE trading day, whichever is later, per Rule 100(a)(2).
Confirm every earnings call was preceded by a press release furnished on Form 8-K Item 2.02 and was open to the public by webcast and dial-in.
Record an exception wherever material information reached a selected audience first without a timed cure.
checklist.done: every investor interaction is logged with pre-cleared materials and each inadvertent disclosure has a timed public cure inside the Rule 100(a)(2) window.

checklist.step: Test the say-on-pay and vote-frequency controls
actions: Confirm the definitive proxy included the separate Rule 14a-21(a) advisory vote on named executive officer compensation and the Item 402 disclosure it relates to.
Recompute the vote cycle - an advisory say-on-pay vote at least once every three years and a say-on-frequency vote at least once every six years since the last one.
Confirm the voting results were reported on Form 8-K Item 5.07 within 4 business days of the meeting and that the frequency decision was reported no later than 150 calendar days after the meeting.
Trace the certified results from the inspector of election to the Item 5.07 figures for, against, abstentions and broker non-votes.
checklist.done: the vote cycle is recomputed as compliant and the certified results agree to the filed Item 5.07 figures.

checklist.step: Execute testing on the financial-reporting key controls in the plan
actions: Draw each sample from the complete period population and record the population source, the extract date and the selection method on the test line.
Test each item against every written attribute and attach the evidence - approval screenshot, reconciliation, journal support - to the sample line.
Obtain the process owner's written explanation for every deviation before concluding and expand to a double sample only where the plan allows.
Set the control conclusion in AuditBoard and route failures to the deficiency log immediately rather than at cycle close.
checklist.done: each planned control has an attribute-level conclusion with attached evidence and failures already routed to the deficiency log.

checklist.step: Hold the exception clearance meeting with the control owners
actions: Circulate the draft exception list to each control owner at least 5 business days before the meeting with the specific items and attributes that failed.
In the meeting obtain either an accepted-as-stated position or a documented rebuttal with evidence attached; never leave an exception in dispute without a written position.
Update the list for accepted rebuttals and record the evidence reference that overturned each one.
Publish the cleared exception list to the SOX Program Manager and the external auditor the same week.
checklist.done: every exception is either accepted by the owner or overturned with attached evidence and the cleared list is shared with the auditor.

checklist.step: Rate each deficiency and decide whether a disclosure is affected
actions: Rate each deficiency on magnitude and likelihood and classify it as a control deficiency, a significant deficiency or a material weakness.
Rate a missed or late waiver disclosure separately as a disclosure-controls deficiency under Rule 13a-15(b) because it affects information required in a 10-K or 8-K.
Escalate anything that could change the Item 9A disclosure-controls conclusion to the Disclosure Committee within 2 business days.
Record the compensating controls considered and why they do or do not reduce the severity.
checklist.done: each deficiency has a severity rating, a documented compensating-control assessment and a disclosure-impact decision.

checklist.step: Build the remediation plan with owners and dated actions
actions: For each deficiency write the corrective action in operational terms - the control redesign, the system change, the training or the added review step - not as a restatement of the failure.
Name a single accountable owner at director level or above and a target date leaving at least three post-remediation control occurrences before year end.
Where the fix is a system change, raise the change ticket and link it to the finding so closure requires evidence of deployment.
Configure an automatic escalation to the CAE when a remediation date slips by more than 15 days.
checklist.done: every deficiency has a concrete corrective action, a named senior owner, a dated plan and a slip escalation rule.

checklist.step: Retest remediated controls from a clean post-remediation population
actions: Confirm the remediation went live on a documented date and that the control has operated at least three times since for a monthly control.
Draw a fresh sample only from occurrences after the go-live date and never reuse the failed original items.
Test the original attributes plus any attribute added by the redesign and record the retest conclusion separately from the original test.
Close the finding only on a clean retest; a partial pass keeps the finding open with a revised date.
checklist.done: each remediated control has a clean retest from a post-go-live population or the finding stays open with a revised date.

checklist.step: Refresh code-of-ethics acknowledgement and training coverage
actions: Run the annual code acknowledgement campaign in the learning management system to all employees, officers and directors with a stated completion deadline.
Reconcile the assignment list to the HRIS active headcount at the campaign date plus the director roster from the board portal so nobody is missed.
Chase non-completers weekly through their HR business partner and escalate anyone still open after 30 days to their executive.
Confirm 100% completion for the CEO, CFO and principal accounting officer specifically, because Item 406 targets those roles.
File the completion report as evidence for the entity-level control.
checklist.done: acknowledgement is reconciled to headcount and the director roster with 100% completion evidenced for the covered officers.

checklist.step: Report results and open items to the Audit Committee
actions: Prepare the Audit Committee pack showing controls tested versus planned, exception counts by process, severity ratings and remediation status with ageing.
Report separately every code-of-ethics waiver granted in the period and whether it was disclosed within 4 business days.
Hold an executive session with the committee without management present, as the listing standards contemplate, and minute that it occurred.
Load the pack to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting and record the committee's directions in the follow-up log.
checklist.done: the committee receives a plan-versus-actual pack including every waiver and its disclosure timing and directions are logged.

checklist.step: Feed the results into the annual Item 406 and Item 9A disclosures
actions: Draft the Item 406 disclosure naming the code, the officers covered, the availability method and the exact investor-relations URL, then confirm the link resolves.
Give the Disclosure Committee the list of waivers granted with their 8-K accession numbers so the periodic report is consistent with the 8-K record.
Provide the deficiency summary to the CEO and CFO for the Rule 13a-15(b) disclosure-controls conclusion supporting the 302 certification.
File the final disclosure package and the test conclusion memo in the financial reporting repository against the fiscal year.
checklist.done: the Item 406 disclosure is drafted with a working URL and is consistent with the filed 8-K waiver record and the disclosure-controls conclusion.

checklist.step: Archive the annual test file for the retention period
actions: Lock the AuditBoard workspace for the year so samples and conclusions cannot be edited after the conclusion date.
Export the test plan, populations, samples, evidence, exception log, remediation retests and the conclusion memo into a single year binder.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index the binder by fiscal year, control id and finding id.
Run a test retrieval and confirm the binder returns within one business day.
checklist.done: the locked annual binder is archived with a 7-year label and proven retrievable by control and finding id.

testing.step: Build the population of controls that should have been tested and waivers that should have been reported
actions: Export the approved annual test plan and the actual tested-control list from AuditBoard and identify every planned control with no completed test.

Extract every ethics case, conflict disclosure and related-party approval for the year from the GRC platform to build the candidate waiver population independently of the ethics team's own classification.
Pull the full 8-K filing index for the year from EDGAR and isolate every Item 5.05 filing.
Reconcile the three populations and list every difference before any sampling begins.
testing.done: planned versus tested controls and candidate waivers versus filed Item 5.05 8-Ks are reconciled with every difference listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the tested populations to their sources of record
actions: Agree the key-control population used for testing to the ICFR control matrix at the year-end lock date and to the Audit Committee approved plan.
Agree the acknowledgement population to the HRIS active headcount at the campaign date plus the board portal director roster.
Agree the investor interaction log to the Investor Relations calendar and the published earnings call transcripts for the year.
Document each reconciling item with its reason and confirm none removes a required control or person from scope.
testing.done: every tested population ties to an independent source of record with reconciling items explained.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across controls, waivers and disclosures
actions: Take 100% of waiver candidates, 100% of logged Regulation FD incidents and 100% of controls with a prior-year deficiency.
Draw 25 further tested controls at random with a recorded seed, stratified so each process appears at least once.
Record the population sizes, the seed, the draw date and the stratification in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm no sampled item was tested, approved or authored by the reviewer performing this test.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all waivers and FD incidents and carries no self-review.

testing.step: Reperform the code-of-ethics disclosure judgement independently
actions: Read Item 406 and reach your own conclusion on whether each sampled ethics case is an implicit or explicit waiver for an executive officer or director, before reading Internal Audit's classification.
Compare to the recorded classification; a case reclassified from waiver to routine approval without a written legal rationale is an exception.
Open the posted code from the investor site yourself and test the Item 406(b) content elements against the current text.
Confirm the 10-K disclosure method matches what the company actually does - a disclosed URL that does not resolve is a fail, not a housekeeping item.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent waiver determination and the posted code and disclosed URL are independently verified.

testing.step: Trace each waiver to its board approval and its EDGAR filing
actions: For each waiver open the board or committee minutes in the board portal and confirm the approval, the approval date and the individual covered.
Search EDGAR for the corresponding Form 8-K and record the accession number, the filing date and the Item 5.05 text.
Confirm the 8-K describes the nature of the waiver, the name of the person and the date as Item 5.05 requires, rather than a generic statement.
Where the website-posting alternative was used, confirm the 10-K disclosed that intention in advance and capture the dated posting.
testing.done: every waiver traces to a minuted approval and a specific Item 5.05 filing or a pre-disclosed dated website posting.

testing.step: Recompute the 4-business-day and vote-cycle deadline maths
actions: For each waiver recompute the business days from board approval to the 8-K filing date, excluding weekends and federal holidays, and compare to the 4-business-day limit.
Recompute the years since the last say-on-pay advisory vote against the 3-year maximum and the years since the last frequency vote against the 6-year maximum.

Recompute the Item 5.07 filing date against the 4-business-day requirement from the shareholder meeting date and, where the frequency decision was reported separately, against the 150-day requirement.
Route any recomputed breach to General Counsel the same day as a reportable disclosure failure rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every deadline is independently recomputed and breaches are routed to General Counsel the same day.

testing.step: Verify the quality of the original control testing on the sample
actions: Compare each sampled control's actual sample size to the frequency table in the approved test plan and flag under-sampling.
Re-run the population extract used for the selection and confirm it covered the full period rather than only the interim months.
Reperform the test on 3 fresh items per sampled control and compare your conclusion to the recorded one.
Treat a control tested from an incomplete population or with an undocumented attribute set as untested.
testing.done: sample sizes, population completeness and conclusions are independently reperformed for every sampled control.

testing.step: Test that remediation fixed the control rather than the paperwork
actions: For each closed finding obtain evidence of the design change - the amended procedure, the deployed change ticket, the added approval step.
Confirm the retest sample was drawn wholly from the post-go-live period and that no failed original item was reused.
Confirm the control had enough post-remediation occurrences before closure and that the retest was performed by someone other than the remediation owner.
Reopen any finding closed on evidence that is only an updated procedure document with no operating evidence.
testing.done: each closed finding is supported by a deployed design change and a clean post-go-live retest by an independent tester.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the control or waiver id, what failed, the day count where a deadline was missed and the disclosure impact.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list - waiver not recognised as a waiver, late board approval, 8-K not triggered, planned control not tested, sample too small, remediation closed without operating evidence - and an owner.
Set the remediation date before the next quarterly close and escalate any missed Item 5.05 filing to General Counsel and the Audit Committee chair the same day.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test plan as a mandatory retest line.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with root cause, day count, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude the test, obtain independent sign-off and report it
actions: Compute the exception rate for the control-testing sample and state the waiver-control result against the zero-tolerance threshold separately.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective - citing the workpaper reference behind each supporting result.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither tested the sampled controls nor approved any sampled waiver, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the waiver disclosure timing record and open findings to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the separate waiver-control result and the exception rate, and is reported and archived.

Accountable obligation owner.value: The Audit Committee is the accountable body under Exchange Act 10A(m); the Board Governance Lead administers the independence and rotation file, drives the PCAOB Rule 3526 letters and maintains the partner rotation clock on behalf of the committee chair

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - SOX 203 and Exchange Act 10A(j) (15 U.S.C. 78j-1(j)) five-year lead and concurring partner rotation, Reg S-X Rule 2-01 (17 CFR 210.2-01) independence criteria and the (c)(6) rotation table, SOX 201 prohibited services, SOX 202 pre-approval and SOX 206 employment cooling-off, re-read on eCFR at each engagement approval together with PCAOB Rules 3520 to 3526

In-scope processes.value: Annual auditor engagement and re-appointment, quarterly pre-approval of all audit, audit-related, tax and other services firmwide including subsidiaries and captives, partner rotation tracking for the lead and concurring partners and the engagement quality reviewer, and the hiring screen for any finance candidate coming from the audit firm

In-scope systems.value: The board portal holds the pre-approval schedule, the Rule 3526 independence letters and the rotation register; Coupa purchase requisitions are blocked for the audit firm vendor id until an approval reference is entered, and fees are tracked by service category in the GL

Compliance procedure documented.value: Auditor Independence and Pre-Approval Policy - the prohibited services list, the general pre-approval categories with dollar caps, the specific pre-approval route, the delegation to the committee chair between meetings, the partner rotation clock rules and the cooling-off hiring screen

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee and re-approved annually at the meeting that appoints the auditor; the CFO and General Counsel countersign, and any change to the dollar caps is minuted

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: PCAOB Rule 3526 independence letter and discussion before initial engagement and at least annually thereafter; pre-approval obtained before any service starts; five consecutive fiscal years maximum for the lead and concurring partners with a five-year time-out for the lead and three years for the concurring partner; PCAOB Form AP filed by the firm within 35 days of the audit report filing date; audit and non-audit fees by category disclosed in the proxy under Item 9(e) of Schedule 14A

Deadline reminders configured.value: Rotation register alerts the committee chair and the CFO 24, 12 and 6 months before a partner reaches year five so a successor can shadow the final year; a quarterly reminder 10 business days before each Audit Committee meeting drives the pre-approval schedule refresh; an annual reminder 60 days before the engagement letter renewal requests the Rule 3526 letter

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Engagement letters, Rule 3526 independence letters, pre-approval schedules and minutes, the partner rotation register, the fee analysis by category and the cooling-off screening records retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any service started without pre-approval, any partner over the rotation limit and any prohibited-service engagement is logged as an independence exception with the fee amount, the remediation and whether the firm concluded its objectivity was impaired

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every independence exception disposition and, with the committee chair, decides whether an impairment assessment and a disclosure are required before the next filing

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every engagement of the audit firm and its network firms by any group entity in the fiscal year, every partner and senior manager assigned to the engagement with their year count, every finance hire from the audit firm in the year, and the fee totals by category feeding the proxy

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - one service performed without prior pre-approval, one prohibited service, or one partner in a sixth consecutive year is a fail regardless of fee size; the Rule 2-01(c)(7) de minimis exception is only available where the services were under 5% of total fees paid, were not recognised as non-audit at engagement and were approved before completion

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per engagement, so pre-approval completeness is tested every quarter against the fee ledger and the rotation and independence file is tested annually before the auditor re-appointment vote

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit tests the pre-approval and rotation controls; the reviewer must not sit on the engagement team interface and must not have requested any sampled non-audit service

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual independence testing workpaper - fee population, pre-approval matching, rotation recomputation, cooling-off screen results and exceptions - filed in the compliance evidence repository and summarised in the Audit Committee minutes

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The independence file - engagement letters, Rule 3526 letters, pre-approval minutes, rotation register, fee analysis and Form AP references - producible to an SEC comment letter or a PCAOB inspection within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: General Counsel owns SEC and PCAOB correspondence on independence; the Audit Committee chair is briefed before any response and clears any disclosure that a service impaired independence

checklist.step: Refresh the auditor engagement and confirm the appointment authority
actions: Draft the Audit Committee resolution appointing the registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year, recording that the committee alone appoints, compensates and oversees the auditor under Exchange Act 10A(m)(2).

Obtain the draft engagement letter from the firm and have General Counsel strike any clause that limits liability, requires arbitration or indemnifies the firm, since such terms can impair independence.
Confirm the scope covers the integrated audit of the financial statements and, where 404(b) applies, ICFR, plus all statutory and subsidiary audits.
Load the executed letter to the board portal against the meeting at which it was approved.
checklist.done: a minuted committee appointment and a countersigned engagement letter free of indemnity and liability-limiting clauses are on the board portal.

checklist.step: Obtain and discuss the PCAOB Rule 3526 independence letter
actions: Request from the engagement partner the written communication describing all relationships between the firm, its network firms and the company that may reasonably bear on independence.
Confirm the letter contains the affirmative statement that the firm is independent within the meaning of the federal securities laws and PCAOB rules.
Schedule the discussion with the Audit Committee, capture the questions asked and the answers given, and minute the committee's conclusion on independence.
Chase the letter if it has not arrived 30 days before the meeting that approves the annual engagement.
File the signed letter and the minute extract in the independence file.
checklist.done: a signed Rule 3526 letter exists for the year, was discussed at a minuted committee meeting and is filed with the discussion record.

checklist.step: Maintain the partner rotation register for every covered person
actions: Ask the firm for the name, role and first year on the engagement for the lead engagement partner, the concurring or engagement quality review partner, and every other audit partner including subsidiary and statutory audit partners.

Record on the rotation register each person's consecutive fiscal years served, the year they must roll off, and the time-out length - five years for the lead partner, three years for the concurring partner, two years for other audit partners after seven years.
Confirm partial years count as full years for the clock where the partner acted as lead for any part of the audit.
Have the engagement partner confirm the register in writing each year rather than relying on internal recollection.
checklist.done: a firm-confirmed register shows every audit partner's consecutive years, roll-off year and required time-out length.

checklist.step: Plan the successor partner transition a year before roll-off
actions: Where a partner reaches year four, ask the firm to propose two successor candidates with insurance-sector experience and PCAOB inspection history.
Interview the candidates with the Audit Committee chair and record the committee's selection in the minutes.
Agree a shadowing plan for the final year covering reserving, reinsurance and investment valuation so continuity does not become a reason to extend.
Confirm the outgoing partner has no consulting, review or advisory role on the engagement during the time-out period.
checklist.done: a committee-selected successor is named and shadowing before year five, with the outgoing partner excluded from the engagement during time-out.

checklist.step: Publish and gate the prohibited non-audit services list
actions: Publish the SOX 201 prohibited list to Procurement and every finance and actuarial leader: bookkeeping, financial information systems design and implementation, appraisal or valuation, actuarial services relating to amounts recorded in the financial statements, internal audit outsourcing, management or human resources functions, broker-dealer or investment banking, legal services and unrelated expert services.
Flag the actuarial prohibition specifically because reserve and DAC support work is the most common breach in an insurer.
Set a hard block in Coupa on the audit firm vendor ids so no requisition can be raised without an Audit Committee pre-approval reference.
Brief Procurement and the FP&A leads each year on how to route a request and what will be refused.
checklist.done: the prohibited list is published, the actuarial prohibition is called out, and procurement is hard-blocked without a pre-approval reference.

checklist.step: Build the annual general pre-approval schedule with dollar caps
actions: Collect from the Controller, the Tax Director and the entity finance leads the expected services for the year by category - audit, audit-related, tax and all other.
Describe each service specifically enough that the committee is not delegating its judgement, and set a dollar cap per service and per category.
Present the schedule to the Audit Committee at the first-quarter meeting and record the approval, the caps and the delegation to the chair for interim approvals up to a stated limit.
Publish the approved schedule to Procurement and Finance and load it to the board portal.
checklist.done: a committee-approved schedule names each service with a dollar cap and records the chair's interim delegation limit.

checklist.step: Run specific pre-approval for anything outside the schedule
actions: Require a pre-approval request form for every service outside the general schedule or above its cap, stating the scope, the fee, the requesting entity and why the service is not prohibited.
Attach the firm's written confirmation that performing the service will not impair independence under Rule 2-01(b) and the four general standards.
Route to the Audit Committee chair under the delegation for interim approval and report every chair approval to the full committee at its next meeting for ratification.
Issue the approval reference that unlocks the Coupa requisition and record it against the engagement.
checklist.done: every out-of-schedule service has a documented request, a firm non-impairment confirmation, an approval and a reference recorded before work starts.

checklist.step: Track fees by category against the approvals every quarter
actions: Extract all vendor spend for the audit firm and its network firms across every group entity for the quarter from the GL and accounts payable ledger.
Map each invoice to audit, audit-related, tax or all other fees using the service description and the approval reference, not the cost centre.
Compare cumulative spend by service to its approved cap and flag any overrun before the next invoice is paid.
Compute the ratio of non-audit fees to total fees and report it to the Audit Committee with the quarterly pre-approval update.
checklist.done: quarterly fees are categorised, matched to approvals, tested against caps and reported with the non-audit fee ratio.

checklist.step: Screen every finance hire coming from the audit firm
actions: Add a mandatory question to the offer workflow asking whether the candidate worked for the company's audit firm in the last two years and in what role.

Where the answer is yes, hold the offer and refer to General Counsel to apply SOX 206 and Rule 2-01(c)(2)(iii): a member of the audit engagement team may not become CEO, CFO, controller, chief accounting officer or an equivalent role within one year of participating in the audit.
Compute the cooling-off period from the start of the audit procedures the person participated in for the period covered by the most recent audit, and record the earliest permitted start date.
Log the screening outcome against the requisition in the HRIS so it is retrievable at audit.
checklist.done: every finance offer carries a documented audit-firm screening and any covered hire has a computed earliest permitted start date.

checklist.step: Test the firm's own independence confirmations at entity level
actions: Send the firm the complete legal entity list including captives, dormant entities, joint ventures and newly acquired subsidiaries, and ask it to confirm no network firm holds a prohibited relationship with any of them.
Ask specifically about business relationships, loans, insurance policies the firm holds with the company, and any investment held by covered persons.
Confirm the firm's audit committee communications cover employment of former firm personnel by the company in financial reporting oversight roles.
Record any relationship identified and the firm's safeguard, and take it to the committee.
checklist.done: the firm has confirmed independence against the complete entity list and every identified relationship has a recorded safeguard.

checklist.step: Confirm the Form AP filing and the engagement partner disclosure
actions: After the 10-K is filed, search the PCAOB AuditorSearch database for the company's Form AP and record the filing date.
Recompute the deadline as 35 days from the date the audit report was first included in a filing and confirm the firm met it.
Confirm the engagement partner named on Form AP matches the partner on the rotation register and the one who signed the audit committee communications.
Confirm any other accounting firm participating in 5% or more of total audit hours is disclosed and that its use was approved by the committee.
checklist.done: Form AP is located, the 35-day deadline is recomputed as met, and the named partner and participating firms reconcile to internal records.

checklist.step: Prepare the fee and pre-approval disclosure for the proxy
actions: Build the four-category fee table for the two most recent fiscal years from the categorised fee ledger and agree the totals to accounts payable.
Draft the Item 9(e) narrative describing the pre-approval policies and procedures and confirm it matches the policy actually in force.
Disclose the percentage of services in each non-audit category approved under the Rule 2-01(c)(7)(i)(C) de minimis exception, and state zero where none were.
Have the Audit Committee chair review the table and narrative before the proxy is typeset and filed.
checklist.done: a fee table agreed to accounts payable and a pre-approval narrative matching the live policy are reviewed by the committee chair.

checklist.step: Receive the AS 1301 communications and the independence discussion at year end
actions: Confirm the auditor delivered the required communications: the planned scope and timing, significant accounting policies and estimates, uncorrected and corrected misstatements, disagreements with management and any difficulties encountered.
Confirm the critical audit matters expected in the opinion were discussed with the committee before the report was issued.
Confirm the annual Rule 3526 independence reaffirmation was delivered and discussed in executive session without management present.
File the communications pack and the minutes on the board portal against the year-end meeting.
checklist.done: all AS 1301 communications and the year-end independence reaffirmation are received, discussed in executive session and minuted.

checklist.step: Take the re-appointment recommendation to the committee and the shareholders
actions: Prepare the annual auditor evaluation covering quality of service, sector expertise, PCAOB inspection results, fee reasonableness and independence record.
Present the evaluation and the rotation position to the Audit Committee and record the re-appointment decision and its rationale.

Prepare the shareholder ratification proposal for the proxy and the Audit Committee Report required by Item 407(d)(3) stating that the committee discussed independence and received the Rule 3526 letter.
After the meeting, confirm the ratification result is reported on Form 8-K Item 5.07 within 4 business days.
checklist.done: a documented evaluation supports a minuted re-appointment, and the committee report and ratification result are filed.

checklist.step: Archive the independence file and set the next year's clock
actions: Assemble the year's file: engagement letter, Rule 3526 letters, pre-approval schedule and minutes, all specific approvals, the fee analysis, the rotation register and the cooling-off screening log.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by fiscal year, partner name and service category.
Roll the rotation register forward one year and confirm the alerts for partners reaching years three, four and five are armed.
Confirm a test retrieval by partner name returns the register within one business day.
checklist.done: the year's independence file is archived under a 7-year label and the rotation clock and alerts are rolled forward and armed.

testing.step: Build the complete population of audit firm engagements and fees
actions: Extract all accounts payable transactions for the fiscal year filtered by every vendor id belonging to the audit firm and its network firms, across every legal entity in the consolidation.
Add accrued but unbilled fees from the year-end accrual schedule so late-billed services cannot escape the population.
Search the contracts repository for any statement of work naming the firm, to catch services procured outside the blocked vendor ids.
Reconcile the total to the fee table drafted for the proxy and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: a complete engagement and fee population is built across all entities and reconciles to the drafted proxy fee table.

testing.step: Reconcile the fee population to the pre-approval record
actions: Match every invoice and statement of work to a general pre-approval schedule line or a specific approval reference in the board portal.
Confirm the approval date precedes the service start date shown on the engagement letter or the first timesheet, not merely the invoice date.
List every unmatched item and every item where approval post-dates the service start as an automatic exception.
Test whether any unapproved item qualifies for the Rule 2-01(c)(7) de minimis exception by computing it as a percentage of total fees paid in the year.
testing.done: every fee traces to an approval that pre-dates the service start, or is an exception with the de minimis test computed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of engagements and covered persons
actions: Take 100% of non-audit engagements, 100% of engagements at newly acquired entities and 100% of partners in their fourth year or later.
Draw 15 further audit and audit-related engagements at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population.
Record the population size, the seed, the draw date and the stratification so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Confirm no sampled engagement was requested or approved by the reviewer performing this test.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all non-audit engagements and late-year partners, and carries no self-review.

testing.step: Reperform the prohibited-service judgement on the sampled non-audit work
actions: Read the actual scope of work for each sampled non-audit engagement rather than the invoice description, which is often generic.
Test the scope against the SOX 201 prohibited categories and reach your own conclusion before reading the approval rationale.
Pay particular attention to any work touching reserve estimation, DAC, actuarial assumptions, valuation of investments or internal audit support at an insurance subsidiary.
Treat a service correctly approved but wrongly categorised - tax work that is really valuation, for example - as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled non-audit scope has an independent prohibited-service conclusion based on the work performed, not the invoice wording.

testing.step: Recompute the partner rotation clocks against the firm's confirmation
actions: Obtain the firm's written confirmation of partner assignments and independently recompute consecutive fiscal years for the lead partner, the concurring partner and each other audit partner.
Test the lead and concurring partners against the five-consecutive-year maximum in Exchange Act 10A(j) and Rule 2-01(c)(6), and other audit partners against the seven-year maximum.
Recompute the time-out for any partner who rotated off - five years for the lead, three for the concurring, two for other audit partners - and confirm no such partner is back on the engagement.
Trace the current lead partner's name to the PCAOB Form AP and to the signature on the audit committee communications.
testing.done: every partner year count and time-out is recomputed and the lead partner reconciles to Form AP and the committee communications.

testing.step: Verify the Rule 3526 letters and the committee's discussion of them
actions: Confirm a written Rule 3526 communication exists for the year and, for any new engagement, one dated before the engagement was accepted.
Confirm the letter lists relationships rather than only asserting independence, and read each disclosed relationship against Rule 2-01(c).
Trace the committee discussion to a specific minute with the date, the attendees, the questions asked and the conclusion reached.
Treat a letter received but never discussed, or discussed only in the management session, as an exception.
testing.done: the Rule 3526 letters exist, list relationships, and each traces to a minuted committee discussion with a stated conclusion.

testing.step: Test the cooling-off screen on finance hires
actions: Extract every hire and internal promotion during the year into a financial reporting oversight role - CFO, controller, chief accounting officer, financial reporting director and equivalents at material subsidiaries.
Cross-check each name against the audit firm's engagement team lists for the prior two years supplied by the firm, not only against the candidate's own declaration.
For any match, recompute the one-year cooling-off period from the start of the audit procedures they participated in and compare it to their start date.
Escalate any hire inside the cooling-off window to General Counsel immediately as a potential independence impairment for the whole audit.
testing.done: every financial reporting oversight hire is cross-checked to the firm's engagement team lists with cooling-off periods recomputed.

testing.step: Recompute the fee table and the de minimis percentages as disclosed
actions: Rebuild the four-category fee table for both disclosed years from the invoice population and compare each figure to the filed proxy.
Recompute the percentage of audit-related, tax and other fees approved under the de minimis exception and compare to the disclosed percentages.
Confirm fees for subsidiary statutory audits and for services to employee benefit plans are captured in the right category and not omitted.
Report any difference above the disclosure rounding threshold to the Corporate Secretary before the proxy is filed, or as a prior-period correction if already filed.
testing.done: the disclosed fee table and de minimis percentages are independently rebuilt and agree to the invoice population.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the entity, the engagement, the fee, what rule was implicated and whether independence may be impaired.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list - service started before approval, procurement block bypassed, scope miscategorised, rotation clock not updated, cooling-off screen skipped, subsidiary engagement not visible - and an owner.
For any potential impairment, open a formal assessment with General Counsel and the firm and record whether the committee concluded independence was maintained.
Set a remediation date before the next quarterly pre-approval cycle and carry the issue forward as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with rule reference, root cause, owner, remediation date and an impairment assessment where relevant.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: State the results against the zero-tolerance threshold: services without pre-approval, prohibited services, partners over the rotation limit and cooling-off breaches, each with a count.
Write the conclusion - independence controls effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who requested and approved none of the sampled services, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee before the re-appointment vote and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states counts against each zero-tolerance criterion and is reported before the re-appointment vote and archived.
