checklist.step: Publish the close-to-file calendar for the reporting year
actions: Compute the statutory due date for each periodic report from the fiscal year end and the current filer status - 60, 75 or 90 days for the 10-K and 40 or 45 days for each 10-Q - and adjust any date falling on a weekend or federal holiday to the next business day.
Work backwards to set the internal milestones: close complete, audit or review clearance, Disclosure Committee meeting, tie-out complete, certification execution and EDGAR submission.
Circulate the calendar to the Controller, Tax, Actuarial, Investor Relations, Legal and the engagement partner and obtain their confirmation of the dates.
Load the milestones into the reporting calendar with T-45 to T-1 alerts and name a single owner per milestone.
checklist.done: a confirmed calendar shows the computed statutory due dates, dated internal milestones with owners, and armed reminders.

checklist.step: Close the books and lock the consolidated trial balance
actions: Confirm every entity has submitted its reporting package and that all intercompany balances and reinsurance eliminations clear to zero in the consolidation tool.
Confirm all balance sheet reconciliations are certified in BlackLine with no unexplained reconciling item above the threshold, and that aged items have documented action plans.
Post and review the top-side consolidation entries with support attached, and confirm the reserve figures agree to the actuarial reserve report signed by the Appointed Actuary.
Lock the ledger period and issue the final consolidated trial balance as the single source for the statements, the schedules and the XBRL tagging.
checklist.done: the period is locked and a single final consolidated trial balance is issued with reconciliations certified and reserves agreed to the actuarial report.

checklist.step: Prepare the financial statements and the Regulation S-X Article 7 schedules
actions: Build the balance sheet, income statement, comprehensive income, equity and cash flow statements from the locked trial balance with a documented mapping from account to caption.

Prepare the Article 7 schedules an insurer must file: Schedule I summary of investments other than investments in related parties, Schedule II condensed financial information of the registrant, Schedule III supplementary insurance information, Schedule IV reinsurance and Schedule V valuation and qualifying accounts.
Prepare the loss and loss adjustment expense reserve roll-forward and the ten-year development table required for property-casualty underwriters.
Agree each schedule to the trial balance and to the reserving platform output and record the agreement in the tie-out binder.
checklist.done: the statements and every required Article 7 schedule are prepared and agreed line by line to the locked trial balance.

checklist.step: Run the disclosure checklist across Regulation S-K and S-X
actions: Work the current-year disclosure checklist item by item through Form 10-K Parts I to IV, marking each item satisfied, not applicable with a reason, or open with an owner.
Confirm the risk factors under Item 105 were refreshed against the year's events and are not repeated verbatim from last year.
Confirm Item 303 MD&A covers results of operations, liquidity and capital resources with the required critical accounting estimates discussion for reserves and investment valuation.
Confirm the Item 601 exhibit index is complete, including the auditor consent as Exhibit 23.1, the subsidiaries list as 21.1 and the clawback policy as Exhibit 97.
Hand every open item to its owner with a date ahead of the Disclosure Committee meeting.
checklist.done: every checklist item is marked satisfied or not applicable with a reason, and the exhibit index is complete.

checklist.step: Assemble the auditor communications and clear the audit
actions: Deliver the final statements, schedules and the tie-out binder to the engagement team and hold the clearance call.
Sign and deliver the management representation letter dated the same day as the audit report, covering completeness of records, litigation, subsequent events, reserves and related parties.
Obtain the schedule of corrected and uncorrected misstatements and take the summary of unadjusted differences to the Audit Committee with the materiality assessment.
Confirm the critical audit matters in the draft opinion are consistent with the disclosures in the statements and raise any inconsistency before the opinion is signed.
Obtain the signed audit report and the Exhibit 23.1 consent.
checklist.done: a signed audit report and consent are received against a dated representation letter, with unadjusted differences taken to the committee.

checklist.step: Hold the Disclosure Committee review before typesetting
actions: Circulate the complete draft including MD&A, risk factors, statements, schedules and exhibits to the committee at least 5 business days before the meeting.
Take each functional lead - Actuarial, Claims, Investments, Legal, IT security, Investor Relations - through the sections they must confirm, and minute their confirmations.
Resolve every open comment in the meeting or assign it with a date before the filing gate, and record the decision on each unadjusted difference.
Record the committee's recommendation that the report be filed and the basis for the disclosure-controls conclusion.
checklist.done: a minuted Disclosure Committee meeting records functional confirmations, resolved comments and a recommendation to file.

checklist.step: Tie out every number in the document to its source
actions: Tick and tie every figure in the statements, notes, schedules and MD&A back to the locked trial balance, the reserving report, the investment accounting system or an external source.
Cross-cast every table and check that every figure repeated in MD&A matches the statements exactly, including rounding.
Verify prior-period columns agree to the previously filed document and investigate any difference as a potential revision requiring disclosure.
Have a second preparer independently re-tie the primary statements and the reserve development table, and sign the tie-out binder.
checklist.done: a two-person signed tie-out binder shows every figure agreed to source with no unexplained difference.

checklist.step: Tag the filing in Inline XBRL and validate it
actions: Tag the face financials, all notes at the detail level required, the Article 7 schedules and the cover page data in Inline XBRL.
Use standard US-GAAP taxonomy elements wherever one exists and document the rationale for every extension element created.
Run the EDGAR and taxonomy validation suites and clear every error and every calculation inconsistency before submission.
Render the viewer output and read it against the human-readable document to confirm signs, scales, periods and axes are right.
File the validation report in the filing binder as evidence.
checklist.done: the Inline XBRL exhibit validates without error, extensions are justified, and the rendered output matches the document.

checklist.step: Execute the officer certifications
actions: Prepare Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 using the exact Rule 13a-14(a) wording with no additions, deletions or reordering of the numbered paragraphs.
Prepare the Section 906 certifications as furnished Exhibits 32.1 and 32.2.

Circulate the certification support binder to the CEO and CFO cross-referencing each paragraph to the evidence - the disclosure-controls evaluation, the ICFR assessment, the sub-certifications and the Audit Committee communications.
Route for signature in DocuSign dated the filing date and confirm the signatories are the officers actually serving on that date.
checklist.done: certifications are executed in exact rule wording, dated the filing date, and supported by a paragraph-level evidence binder.

checklist.step: Submit the filing on EDGAR and confirm acceptance
actions: Assemble the submission with the correct form type, period of report, CIK and filer credentials, and attach every exhibit including the consent, the certifications and the Inline XBRL files.
Run a test submission first and clear every EDGAR warning before the live filing.
Submit at least 2 hours before the 5:30 pm Eastern cut-off so a rejection can still be corrected the same day.
Retrieve the acceptance message, record the accession number and the filing timestamp, and confirm the document renders correctly on the public EDGAR page.
Notify Investor Relations to release and to post the document to the investor website the same day.
checklist.done: the filing is accepted before the deadline with the accession number and timestamp recorded and the public document verified.

checklist.step: Deliver the annual report to security holders with the proxy
actions: Confirm the annual report required by Rule 14a-3(b) contains the audited statements for the last two fiscal years, the selected financial data required, MD&A and the market information.
Confirm delivery accompanies or precedes the proxy statement and that the notice-and-access materials are posted on the specified website by the required date.
File the annual report to security holders on EDGAR where a paper or electronic copy is furnished under Rule 14a-3(c).
Retain the transfer agent's certificate of mailing or posting as evidence of delivery.
checklist.done: the security holder annual report is complete, delivered no later than the proxy, and delivery is evidenced by the transfer agent.

checklist.step: Handle a threatened late filing through Form 12b-25 rather than filing late
actions: Where a milestone slips such that the deadline is at risk, convene the Controller, General Counsel and the engagement partner within one business day.
If the report genuinely cannot be filed on time, prepare Form 12b-25 stating the reason without unreasonable effort or expense and file it no later than one business day after the original due date.
Note that the extension is 15 calendar days for an annual report and 5 calendar days for a quarterly report, and that the report must be filed within that window to be deemed timely.
Brief Investor Relations and the Audit Committee before the notification is filed, and assess the impact on Form S-3 shelf eligibility and any debt covenant reporting requirement.
checklist.done: a Form 12b-25 is filed within one business day of the original due date with the extension window diarised and the S-3 impact assessed.

checklist.step: Run the post-filing review and close out the cycle
actions: Read the filed document as it appears on EDGAR for pagination, missing exhibits, broken tables and incorrect period headers.
Reconcile the filed figures to the earnings release furnished on Form 8-K Item 2.02 and explain any difference to Investor Relations before analysts find it.
Log any error found and decide with General Counsel whether it warrants a 10-K/A, a correction in the next periodic report or no action, and record the rationale.
Hold the lessons-learned session within 10 business days and update the calendar and checklist for the next cycle.
checklist.done: the filed document is reviewed on EDGAR, reconciled to the earnings release, and every error has a documented disposition.

checklist.step: Respond to SEC staff comments within the letter's deadline
actions: On receipt of a Division of Corporation Finance comment letter, log it, diarise the response date stated in the letter and notify the CFO and the Audit Committee chair the same day.
Assign each comment to the Controller, Actuarial or Legal, and draft a response quoting the comment and giving the proposed revised disclosure in full.
Have the engagement partner review any response touching the audited statements before it is submitted.
Submit the response through EDGAR as correspondence, and where the staff requires it, file an amended report carrying the revised disclosure.
checklist.done: each comment has an owned, auditor-reviewed response submitted by the date the letter set, with any amendment filed.

checklist.step: Archive the filing binder for the retention period
actions: Assemble the binder: locked trial balance, statements and schedules, tie-out, disclosure checklist, Disclosure Committee minutes, representation letter, audit report and consent, certifications, XBRL validation report and the EDGAR acceptance message.
Index the binder by fiscal period, form type and accession number and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the archived document is the exact version accepted by EDGAR by comparing file hashes.
Run a test retrieval by accession number and confirm the binder returns within one business day.
checklist.done: the filing binder is archived under a 7-year label, hash-matched to the accepted EDGAR version and retrievable by accession number.

testing.step: Build the population of periodic reports required and filed
actions: List every Exchange Act periodic report the registrant owed for the year - one 10-K under Rule 13a-1 and one 10-Q per quarter under Rule 13a-13 - plus the Rule 14a-3(b) annual report.
Pull the registrant's complete EDGAR filing index for the year and match each required report to an actual filing with its accession number and timestamp.
Add every amendment, Form 12b-25 and Item 4.02 filing to the population.
List any required report with no matching filing as an automatic exception before any sampling.
testing.done: every required periodic report is matched to a filing on EDGAR, with amendments and notifications captured and gaps listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed statements to the locked general ledger
actions: Pull the locked consolidated trial balance for the period and independently map it to the filed balance sheet and income statement captions.
Agree total assets, total liabilities, equity, revenue and net income to the penny, and investigate any difference regardless of size.
Agree the loss and loss adjustment expense reserve balance to the Appointed Actuary's signed reserve report and to Schedule III.
Document the reconciliation with the source references in the workpaper.
testing.done: the filed primary statements reconcile exactly to the locked trial balance and the reserve balance ties to the actuarial report.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of disclosures, schedules and exhibits
actions: Take 100% of the Article 7 schedules, the reserve development table, the certifications and the auditor consent.
Draw 20 further disclosure checklist items at random with a recorded seed across Parts I to IV of the 10-K.
Record the population size, the seed and the draw date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Confirm no sampled item was prepared or tied out by the reviewer performing this test.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all Article 7 schedules and certifications, and carries no self-review.

testing.step: Reperform the disclosure checklist judgement on the sampled items
actions: Read the current text of the Regulation S-K or S-X item behind each sampled checklist line on eCFR and reach your own conclusion on what the filing must contain.
Locate the corresponding disclosure in the filed document and confirm it satisfies every element of the item, not merely the topic.
Challenge every not applicable marking by asking what fact would make it applicable and whether that fact exists this year.
Treat a stale disclosure carried forward unchanged where the underlying facts moved as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled item has an independent completeness conclusion read against the current rule text, with not-applicable markings challenged.

testing.step: Reperform the tie-out on the sampled figures
actions: Select 40 figures spread across the statements, notes, Article 7 schedules and MD&A and trace each to the trial balance, the reserving report or the investment accounting system.
Cross-cast every sampled table and confirm subtotals and totals foot and cross-foot.
Confirm every figure that appears in more than one place in the document agrees, including the earnings release furnished on Form 8-K Item 2.02.
Log every difference with its magnitude and whether it changes a disclosed subtotal.
testing.done: the sampled figures independently tie to source, tables foot, and repeated figures agree across the document and the release.

testing.step: Validate the Inline XBRL exhibit independently
actions: Download the filed Inline XBRL exhibit from EDGAR and re-run the validation suite yourself rather than relying on the pre-filing report.
Compare 25 tagged values to the human-readable document checking element choice, sign, scale, decimals and period context.
List every extension element used and test whether a standard US-GAAP element existed - an unnecessary extension is an exception.
Confirm the cover page data, including the trading symbol, exchange and filer status boxes, is tagged and correct.
testing.done: the filed XBRL validates independently and sampled tags, extensions and cover page data are verified against the document.

testing.step: Recompute every filing deadline against the acceptance timestamps
actions: Recompute each report's due date from the period end using the filer status on the cover page - 60, 75 or 90 days for the 10-K and 40 or 45 for the 10-Q - rolling weekend and federal holiday dates forward.
Compare each computed date to the EDGAR acceptance timestamp and record the days early or late.
Where a Form 12b-25 was used, confirm it was filed no later than one business day after the original due date and that the report landed inside the 15 or 5 calendar day window.
Treat any filing outside the window as a reportable late filing affecting Form S-3 eligibility, not a test exception.
testing.done: every deadline is independently recomputed against the acceptance timestamp with any 12b-25 window verified.

testing.step: Verify the certifications, consent and auditor communications as filed
actions: Compare the text of Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 word for word to the Rule 13a-14(a) form of certification and flag any altered, added or omitted paragraph.
Confirm the signatories held the principal executive and principal financial officer roles on the filing date by checking the 8-K Item 5.02 history.
Confirm Exhibit 23.1 consent is present, names the correct firm and refers to the correct registration statements.
Confirm the AS 1301 communications and the management representation letter are dated on or before the audit report date.
testing.done: certification text, signatory authority, consent and the dating of auditor communications are all independently verified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the form type, the accession number, the item or figure affected and whether the filed document is wrong.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list - milestone slipped, checklist item skipped, tie-out not reperformed, XBRL tagged from a superseded draft, certification wording altered, deadline miscomputed - and an owner.
For any filed error, record the disposition decision - amendment, correction in the next report, or no action - with the General Counsel rationale attached.
Set remediation dates before the next quarterly filing and carry open issues into the next post-filing review.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with the accession number, root cause, owner, remediation date and a filed-error disposition.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: State the results against each threshold: filings late, tie-out differences, missing schedules or exhibits and XBRL validation errors, each with a count.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective - with the workpaper reference behind each result.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and tied out none of the sampled statements, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at the meeting that reviews the next periodic report and file the signed workpaper in the financial reporting repository against the accession number.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states counts against each threshold and a conclusion, and is reported to the committee and archived by accession number.

checklist.step: Maintain the current board and committee composition record
actions: Keep a single composition record on the board portal listing every director with their appointment date, term, committee memberships, chair roles and independence status.
Update the record the same business day a director is appointed, resigns, changes committees or has a status-changing event, and note what triggered the change.
Recompute after every change whether independent directors remain a majority of the whole board as NYSE 303A.01 requires.
Recompute audit committee size against the three-member minimum and confirm every committee remains fully independent.
checklist.done: the composition record is current to the same business day and majority-independence and committee minimums are recomputed on every change.

checklist.step: Issue and collect the annual director and officer questionnaire
actions: Issue the questionnaire at least 45 days before the annual meeting through DocuSign with a stated return date.

Include questions on employment history for the last three years, family relationships, compensation received from the company other than director fees, relationships with the audit firm, business relationships with the company and their dollar amounts, charitable contributions, and related person transactions.
Chase non-returns weekly and escalate to the board chair anyone outstanding 10 days before the determination meeting.
Store the signed questionnaires in the board portal and flag every affirmative answer for legal review.
checklist.done: every serving director and executive officer has returned a signed questionnaire and each affirmative answer is flagged for review.

checklist.step: Test each director against the bright-line independence disqualifiers
actions: For each director apply the NYSE 303A.02(b) bright lines over the three-year look-back: employment by the company, receipt of more than 120,000 dollars in direct compensation in any twelve-month period other than director fees, employment as or by the internal or external auditor, interlocking compensation committee relationships, and employment by a company doing business above the 2 percent or 1 million dollar of gross revenues test.
For each disqualifier record the tested fact, the amount and the source - questionnaire answer, payroll record, accounts payable data or the auditor's confirmation.
Where a relationship exists but falls below the bright line, apply the board's categorical standards and document why it is not material.
Prepare a memo per director stating the conclusion and the facts behind it, not merely the word independent.
checklist.done: each director has a memo testing every bright line with the amounts and sources shown and a stated conclusion.

checklist.step: Apply the stricter Rule 10A-3 test to every audit committee member
actions: Confirm each audit committee member accepts no consulting, advisory or other compensatory fee from the company or any subsidiary other than board and committee fees, including deferred amounts for prior service.
Confirm no member is an affiliated person of the company or any subsidiary, applying the 10 percent ownership safe harbour and the control analysis.
Extract from accounts payable and payroll any payment to a member or to an entity they own or control and test it against the fee prohibition.
Record the conclusion per member and confirm the committee has at least three members who are also financially literate under the exchange standard.
checklist.done: each audit committee member has a documented Rule 10A-3 conclusion on fees and affiliation, with a literate three-member committee confirmed.

checklist.step: Apply the Rule 10C-1 factors to every compensation committee member
actions: For each compensation committee member consider the source of the director's compensation, including any consulting, advisory or other fee paid by the company, and any affiliate relationship with the company or a subsidiary.
Document the board's affirmative determination of independence for compensation committee service, which is a separate determination from general board independence.
Confirm the committee assessed the independence of every compensation consultant, legal counsel and adviser it retained against the six Rule 10C-1(b)(4) factors, and minute that assessment.
File the determinations and the adviser assessments in the committee's annual record.
checklist.done: each compensation committee member has a separate documented independence determination and every adviser has a minuted six-factor assessment.

checklist.step: Identify and disclose the audit committee financial expert
actions: Test candidates against the Item 407(d)(5)(ii) attributes: understanding of GAAP and financial statements, ability to assess the application of GAAP to estimates and reserves, experience preparing auditing analysing or evaluating comparable financial statements, understanding of internal control over financial reporting and understanding of audit committee functions.
Record which experience gives each attribute, drawn from the director's biography rather than asserted.
Have the board determine and minute who is the audit committee financial expert and whether they are independent.
Where no expert is designated, prepare the required explanation for the proxy rather than leaving the disclosure silent.
checklist.done: a board-minuted financial expert determination exists with each attribute evidenced, or an explanation is prepared for the disclosure.

checklist.step: Keep the committee charters current and evidence what they require
actions: Review each charter annually against the exchange requirements: the audit committee charter must cover its purpose, the auditor appointment and oversight authority, the annual performance evaluation and the duties in NYSE 303A.07(b).

Confirm the compensation committee charter grants sole authority to retain and fund advisers and to determine CEO compensation, and the nominating charter covers director identification, qualification and governance guidelines.
Build a charter requirement tracker listing every duty and the meeting at which it was performed during the year, so nothing sits unperformed.
Post the current charters and the corporate governance guidelines to the investor website and confirm the links resolve.
checklist.done: every charter is annually reviewed, every charter duty is traced to a meeting where it was performed, and the posted versions are current and reachable.

checklist.step: Hold and minute executive sessions of non-management directors
actions: Schedule an executive session of non-management directors at each regularly scheduled board meeting as NYSE 303A.03 requires, and at least annually a session of independent directors only.
Record the presiding director for each session, and confirm the method for selecting the presiding director is disclosed on the website or in the proxy.
Minute that the session occurred, who attended and that management was not present, without minuting the substance where the board prefers.
Confirm the means for interested parties to communicate directly with the presiding director or the non-management directors is published.
checklist.done: each regular meeting has a minuted non-management executive session with a named presiding director and a published communication channel.

checklist.step: Screen every new director candidate before appointment
actions: Have the candidate complete the full questionnaire and a background check covering criminal, regulatory, bankruptcy and litigation history for the last ten years for Item 401(f) purposes.
Run the independence bright lines and, where the candidate will join the audit or compensation committee, the Rule 10A-3 and 10C-1 tests, before the appointment is voted.
Check overboarding against the governance guidelines limit on other public company boards and confirm the candidate can commit the time.
Confirm with the Chief Compliance Officer that appointment does not create a conflict with any insurance regulator requirement applicable to the group's insurance subsidiaries.
checklist.done: no candidate is voted on without a completed questionnaire, background check, independence and committee eligibility testing and an overboarding check.

checklist.step: File the annual written affirmation with the listing exchange
actions: Within 30 days after the annual meeting log in to the NYSE Listing Manager, or the Nasdaq Listing Center, and open the annual written affirmation form.

Complete the sections on board and committee composition, the independence determinations, the audit committee financial expert and the availability of the charters and guidelines, drawing every answer from the composition record.
Attach or affirm the CEO certification that the company is not aware of any violation of the exchange corporate governance listing standards.
Submit, capture the confirmation number and the submission timestamp and file both in the compliance evidence repository against the meeting date.
checklist.done: the annual affirmation is submitted within 30 days of the annual meeting with the confirmation number and timestamp filed.

checklist.step: File an interim written affirmation on any change
actions: Trigger the interim affirmation workflow the moment a director resigns, is appointed, changes committee membership, loses independence or the financial expert designation changes.
Complete and submit the interim written affirmation through the exchange portal within 5 business days of the change and record the elapsed day count.
Confirm the corresponding Form 8-K Item 5.02 was filed within 4 business days where the change involves a director or a principal officer.
Update the composition record, the board portal and the investor website committee listings the same day.
checklist.done: every board or committee change has an interim affirmation inside 5 business days with the day count recorded and the 8-K cross-checked.

checklist.step: Escalate and notify the exchange the moment a standard is breached
actions: Where a resignation drops the board below majority independence or a committee below its required composition, notify the exchange promptly in writing as the listing standards require.

Determine whether an exchange cure period applies - for example the Rule 10A-3(a)(3) cure period where a member ceases to be independent for reasons outside their control - and document the basis for relying on it.
Set the recruitment or reappointment plan with a date inside the cure window and report progress to the board at each meeting.
Prepare the Item 5.02 Form 8-K and any required website disclosure with the Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: each breach has a prompt written notice to the exchange, a documented cure basis and a dated plan inside the cure window.

checklist.step: Run the annual board and committee self-evaluation
actions: Issue the evaluation questionnaire covering board composition, meeting materials, time on strategy and risk, committee effectiveness and executive session usefulness.
Collect responses confidentially, summarise the themes without attribution and present them to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.
Minute the completion of the audit, compensation and nominating committee evaluations, each of which the exchange requires annually.
Record the actions agreed with owners and dates and track them into the next year's governance calendar.
checklist.done: board and each committee evaluation is completed and minuted with agreed actions carrying owners and dates.

checklist.step: Draft the Item 407 governance disclosures for the proxy
actions: Draft the independence disclosure naming each independent director and describing by category any relationship the board considered and found immaterial.
Draft the committee disclosures with membership, number of meetings held during the year taken from the minutes, and the charter availability statement with the website URL.
Draft the board leadership structure and risk oversight discussion required by Item 407(h), including how the board oversees enterprise, cybersecurity and insurance underwriting risk.
Draft the compensation committee interlocks and insider participation disclosure and the audit committee report, and route the whole package to General Counsel and the committee chairs.
checklist.done: each Item 407 subsection is drafted from source records, with meeting counts taken from minutes and chair review evidenced.

checklist.step: Archive the governance file and roll the calendar forward
actions: Assemble the year's file: questionnaires, independence memos, committee eligibility determinations, charters with version history, minutes, evaluation summaries, affirmations and exchange confirmations.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by fiscal year, director name and committee.
Roll the governance calendar forward with the questionnaire issue date, the determination meeting, the annual meeting and the affirmation deadline populated.
Confirm a test retrieval by director name returns the independence memo within one business day.
checklist.done: the governance file is archived under a 7-year label, retrievable by director, and next year's calendar dates are populated.

testing.step: Build the population of directors, committee seats and required affirmations
actions: Extract from the board portal every director serving at any point in the year with appointment and departure dates and every committee seat held with its dates.
Build the timeline of board composition day by day so any period below majority independence is visible rather than only the year-end position.
List every event that should have triggered an interim affirmation and every annual meeting that started a 30-day affirmation clock.
Reconcile the director list to the proxy director slate and to the Form 8-K Item 5.02 filings for the year.
testing.done: a day-by-day composition timeline is built and reconciles to the proxy slate and the Item 5.02 filings.

testing.step: Reconcile the composition record to the corporate and exchange records
actions: Agree the composition record to the signed board minutes for every appointment, resignation and committee change.
Agree the committee membership shown on the investor website and in the proxy to the composition record as of the proxy date.
Agree the affirmations submitted to the exchange to the composition record as of each submission date.
List any record that disagrees and determine which version the exchange and shareholders were given.
testing.done: minutes, website, proxy and exchange affirmations all agree to the composition record, or the differences are identified.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of directors and charter requirements
actions: Take 100% of audit and compensation committee members, 100% of directors appointed or departed during the year and 100% of directors with any affirmative questionnaire answer.
Draw 5 further directors at random with a recorded seed, plus 15 charter duties across the three committees.
Record the population sizes, the seed and the draw date so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm the reviewer prepared none of the sampled independence memos and sits on none of the committees.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all committee members and status changes, and carries no self-review.

testing.step: Reperform the independence determination for each sampled director
actions: Read the current NYSE 303A.02 text, or the Nasdaq 5605(a)(2) equivalent, and apply each bright line yourself to the sampled director before reading the company's memo.

Independently source the amounts rather than relying on the questionnaire - pull payments to the director or their firms from accounts payable, and pull charitable contributions from the giving record.
Recompute the 2 percent of consolidated gross revenues test using the counterparty's published revenues and the payments made in each of the last three fiscal years.
Treat a right answer supported by an untested questionnaire assertion as an exception in evidence even where the conclusion holds.
testing.done: each sampled director has an independently sourced bright-line reperformance with the revenue test recomputed.

testing.step: Reperform the Rule 10A-3 and 10C-1 committee eligibility tests
actions: For each audit committee member, search accounts payable and payroll for any payment in the year to the member or an entity they control and test it against the compensatory fee prohibition.
Test affiliation by pulling the beneficial ownership table from the proxy and checking the 10 percent safe harbour and any control relationship.
For each compensation committee member confirm a separate board determination exists and that the six Rule 10C-1(b)(4) adviser factors were minuted for every adviser retained.
Treat a general board independence determination used as a substitute for either specific test as a fail.
testing.done: every audit and compensation committee member has an independently reperformed eligibility test with the payment search evidenced.

testing.step: Trace sampled charter duties to the meeting where they were performed
actions: For each sampled charter duty, locate the minute recording its performance and note the meeting date and the material reviewed.
Confirm the annually required duties - committee self-evaluation, charter review, auditor appointment, CEO compensation determination, governance guideline review - each occurred in the year.
Confirm the number of committee meetings recorded in the minutes matches the number disclosed in the proxy.
Log any charter duty with no corresponding minute as an exception in governance operation, not only in documentation.
testing.done: every sampled charter duty traces to a dated minute and the disclosed meeting counts agree to the minutes.

testing.step: Recompute the affirmation deadline maths for the year
actions: Recompute the annual affirmation due date as 30 calendar days after the annual meeting date and compare it to the exchange confirmation timestamp.
For each composition change recompute the 5-business-day interim affirmation deadline, excluding weekends and exchange holidays, and compare it to the submission timestamp.
Recompute the 4-business-day Form 8-K Item 5.02 deadline for each director or officer change and compare it to the EDGAR acceptance timestamp.
Record days early or late for every submission and treat any late filing as a listing standard breach for General Counsel.
testing.done: every annual, interim and 8-K deadline is independently recomputed against a timestamp with days early or late recorded.

testing.step: Verify the Item 407 disclosures against the underlying records
actions: Open the filed proxy and check the list of independent directors against the board's minuted determinations, name by name.
Confirm every relationship the board considered and deemed immaterial is described by category as Item 407(a) requires, not omitted.
Confirm the audit committee financial expert disclosure names an actual person and that the board minuted the determination, or that the explanation for having none is present.
Confirm the compensation committee interlocks disclosure reflects the questionnaire answers and the related person transaction record.
testing.done: every Item 407 statement in the filed proxy is traced to a minuted determination or an underlying record.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the director or committee, the standard implicated, the period affected and whether the exchange or shareholders received wrong information.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list - questionnaire not tested to source, composition record not updated on change, interim affirmation not triggered, charter duty not scheduled, disclosure drafted from last year - and an owner.
For any composition breach, record the exchange notice date, the cure basis and the date compliance was restored.
Set remediation dates before the next board meeting and carry open issues into the next annual governance test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with the standard implicated, root cause, owner, remediation date and any exchange notice recorded.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the governance committee
actions: State the results against each zero-tolerance criterion - days below majority independence, committee composition failures, ineligible members and late affirmations - with a count for each.
Write the conclusion - compliant, compliant with exceptions or non-compliant - with the workpaper references behind each result.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no sampled independence memo and no affirmation, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states counts against each criterion and a conclusion, reported to both committees and archived.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Corporate Secretary owns the annual proxy statement, the 10-K Part III governance disclosures and the Section 16 filing service for directors and Section 16 officers; the Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the EDGAR mechanics

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Exchange Act 13(a) with Rule 13a-1, Exchange Act 14(a) with Rule 14a-3 and Schedule 14A (17 CFR 240.14a-101), and Exchange Act 16(a) with Rule 16a-3 (17 CFR 240.16a-3), re-read on eCFR before each proxy season together with the current Schedule 14A item list and the pay versus performance requirements of Item 402(v)

In-scope processes.value: Annual meeting planning and proxy preparation, executive and director compensation disclosure, related person transaction collection and review, beneficial ownership tabulation, Section 16 Forms 3, 4 and 5 preparation and filing for every insider, the Item 5.07 voting results 8-K and the 10-K Part III incorporation by reference

In-scope systems.value: The proxy and 10-K Part III drafts, compensation tables and beneficial ownership schedules are assembled in the financial reporting repository; the board portal holds the questionnaires and minutes; Section 16 forms are submitted on EDGAR with each insider's own CIK and a filed power of attorney

Compliance procedure documented.value: Proxy and Section 16 Procedure - the proxy season calendar, the Schedule 14A item checklist, the compensation table preparation and review steps, the related person transaction questionnaire and committee review, the insider list maintenance rule and the two-business-day Form 4 runbook

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the General Counsel and the Corporate Secretary and reviewed by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee each year before the questionnaires are issued

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Preliminary proxy on Schedule 14A filed at least 10 calendar days before the definitive proxy where required by Rule 14a-6; the definitive proxy filed no later than the date it is first sent to security holders, with notice and access materials posted and the notice sent at least 40 calendar days before the meeting; Form 3 within 10 days of becoming an insider; Form 4 before the end of the second business day following the transaction; Form 5 within 45 days after fiscal year end; 10-K Part III incorporated by reference only if the definitive proxy is filed within 120 days of fiscal year end; Form 8-K Item 5.07 voting results within 4 business days of the meeting

Deadline reminders configured.value: The proxy calendar alerts at T-120, T-60, T-30 and T-10 days to the definitive filing date; the 120-day Part III cut-off is a hard gate on the reporting calendar; every logged insider transaction opens an automatic two-business-day Form 4 countdown to the preparer and the Corporate Secretary; a 45-day post-year-end reminder drives the Form 5 sweep

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Questionnaires, compensation table workpapers, beneficial ownership tabulations, related person transaction reviews and committee minutes, filed proxies, Section 16 forms with their transaction support and powers of attorney, and the inspector of election certificate retained 7 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late or amended Section 16 filings, missed related person transactions and proxy disclosure errors are logged with the insider name, the day count, the cause and whether an Item 405 delinquency disclosure is required in the next proxy

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every late Section 16 filing and its Item 405 disclosure, and approves any proxy supplement or amendment before it is filed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The definitive and any preliminary proxy for the year, the 10-K Part III disclosures, every Section 16 reportable transaction by every director and Section 16 officer, every related person transaction identified, and the Item 5.07 8-K reporting the meeting results

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any Form 4 filed after the second business day, any Form 3 after ten days, any Form 5 after forty-five days, a definitive proxy filed after the date it was first sent, or a Part III incorporation by reference where the proxy landed after the 120th day is a fail; every compensation table figure must tie to source with no unexplained difference

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The proxy obligation is annual and the Section 16 obligation is event-driven, so the proxy disclosure test runs once a year after the definitive filing and the Section 16 timeliness test runs monthly against the transaction log, with a full sweep at the Form 5 deadline

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Compliance reviews the proxy and Section 16 controls independently of the Corporate Secretary's office; no reviewer may have prepared a sampled form or compensation table

Evidence location for test results.value: Proxy season test workpaper - filing timeline, Schedule 14A checklist reperformance, compensation table tie-out, Section 16 timeliness recomputation and exceptions - filed in the compliance evidence repository against the proxy accession number

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The proxy file with the checklist, table workpapers, questionnaires, related person transaction minutes, Section 16 transaction support and EDGAR acceptance messages, producible to a Division of Corporation Finance comment letter within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: General Counsel owns SEC comment letters on the proxy and any Section 16 enforcement inquiry; the Compensation Committee chair reviews any response touching the compensation tables before it is filed

checklist.step: Set the proxy season calendar from the intended meeting date
actions: Fix the annual meeting date with the board and work backwards to the record date under the state corporate law and bylaw notice periods.

Compute the definitive proxy filing date, the notice and access posting date at least 40 calendar days before the meeting, and the preliminary proxy date at least 10 calendar days earlier where Rule 14a-6 requires a preliminary filing.
Add the hard gate at 120 days after fiscal year end for the Part III incorporation by reference and mark it as non-negotiable on the reporting calendar.
Circulate the calendar to Legal, Compensation, Investor Relations, the transfer agent, the proxy solicitor and the financial printer and obtain written confirmation of each date.
checklist.done: a confirmed calendar shows the record date, preliminary and definitive filing dates, the 40-day notice date and the 120-day Part III gate.

checklist.step: Determine whether a preliminary proxy filing is required
actions: List every matter to be voted on and test each against the Rule 14a-6(a) exclusions - election of directors, auditor ratification, say-on-pay and shareholder proposals under Rule 14a-8 do not by themselves require a preliminary filing.

Where any other matter appears, such as an equity plan amendment, a charter amendment or a business combination, prepare and file the preliminary proxy at least 10 calendar days before the definitive.
Record the analysis and the conclusion in the proxy file so the decision is evidenced rather than assumed.
Diarise the staff review window and hold the definitive filing until the 10 calendar days have run or the staff has confirmed no review.
checklist.done: a documented Rule 14a-6 analysis supports either a preliminary filing 10 days ahead or a reasoned decision to file only a definitive proxy.

checklist.step: Collect and review related person transactions
actions: Issue the related person transaction section of the questionnaire to every director, director nominee, executive officer and known 5 percent holder, covering the person and their immediate family.

Independently search the accounts payable and accounts receivable masters and the policyholder and agency records for names matching the related person list, since self-reporting misses group entities.
For each identified transaction record the amount, the relationship, the terms and whether they are at arm's length, and test it against the 120,000 dollar Item 404(a) disclosure threshold.
Take each transaction to the committee designated in the related person transaction policy for approval or ratification and minute the decision.
Draft the Item 404 disclosure and the policy description required by Item 404(b).
checklist.done: related persons are searched against the ledgers as well as self-reported, and each transaction above threshold is committee-reviewed and drafted for disclosure.

checklist.step: Prepare the executive compensation tables
actions: Identify the named executive officers for the year using the Item 402(a)(3) test - the principal executive officer, the principal financial officer and the three other most highly compensated executive officers by total compensation excluding the change in pension value.

Build the Summary Compensation Table pulling salary and bonus from payroll, equity grant date fair values from the equity administration system agreed to the ASC 718 valuation, non-equity incentive payouts from the approved scorecard, pension value change from the actuary and all other compensation from the perquisite log.
Build the Grants of Plan-Based Awards, Outstanding Equity, Option Exercises and Stock Vested, Pension Benefits and Nonqualified Deferred Compensation tables from the same sources.

Compute the CEO pay ratio under Item 402(u) documenting the median employee identification methodology and the consistently applied compensation measure, and the pay versus performance table under Item 402(v) with the compensation actually paid adjustments.
Have a second preparer tie every table figure to source and sign the tie-out.
checklist.done: every compensation table is built from named sources, independently tied out and signed, with the pay ratio and pay versus performance methodologies documented.

checklist.step: Tabulate beneficial ownership as of the record date
actions: Take the record date holdings for each director, nominee, named executive officer and the group from the transfer agent and the equity administration system.
Add shares issuable on options exercisable and restricted stock units vesting within 60 days of the record date, as Rule 13d-3(d)(1) requires, and disclose the component in a footnote.
Identify 5 percent holders from Schedule 13D and 13G filings on EDGAR as of the record date and record the source filing date for each.
Compute each percentage using the denominator of shares outstanding plus that holder's own 60-day shares only, and have a second preparer recompute the table.
checklist.done: the Item 403 table is built from transfer agent and 13D/13G sources with 60-day shares included and percentages independently recomputed.

checklist.step: Work the Schedule 14A item checklist end to end
actions: Work item by item through Schedule 14A: Items 1 to 4 on date time place, revocability, dissenters rights and persons making the solicitation and its cost; Items 5 to 6 on participants and voting securities; Item 7 on directors and Item 8 on compensation; Item 9 on the auditor including the fee table; Item 10 on compensation plans; Item 21 on voting procedures.
Mark each item satisfied with the page reference, or not applicable with the reason.
Confirm the say-on-pay resolution and, where due, the say-on-frequency resolution are included with the required disclosure of the effect of the vote.
Confirm the deadline for Rule 14a-8 shareholder proposals for the next meeting is disclosed, computed as 120 calendar days before the anniversary of the date this proxy is released.
checklist.done: every Schedule 14A item is marked satisfied with a page reference or not applicable with a reason, including next year's 14a-8 deadline.

checklist.step: Maintain the Section 16 insider list and the powers of attorney
actions: Have the board designate the Section 16 officers annually by resolution, applying the Rule 16a-1(f) policy-making function test rather than job titles alone.

For every new insider obtain EDGAR filer credentials - the individual CIK and CCC through EDGAR Next - and a signed power of attorney authorising the Corporate Secretary's office to file on their behalf.
File the Form 3 within 10 days of the person becoming a director or Section 16 officer, showing all holdings even where they hold none.
Remove departing insiders from the list only after their final Form 4 obligations run and document the removal date.
checklist.done: a board-resolved insider list is current, every insider has filing credentials and a power of attorney, and Form 3s were filed within 10 days.

checklist.step: Capture every insider transaction the day it happens
actions: Require pre-clearance for every insider transaction through the trading window procedure and log the request, the approval and the intended trade date.

Take a daily feed from the equity administration system and the designated brokers covering exercises, sales, restricted stock unit vestings, tax withholding, gifts and 401(k) or deferred plan transactions.
Match each feed item to a pre-clearance and chase any unmatched trade with the insider the same day, since the two-business-day clock has already started.
Record the transaction date, the code, the number of shares, the price and the resulting holdings on the insider's transaction ledger.
checklist.done: every insider transaction is captured on trade date from broker and equity system feeds and matched to a pre-clearance.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the Form 4 within two business days
actions: Prepare the Form 4 with Table I for non-derivative and Table II for derivative securities, entering the transaction date, the transaction code, the amount, the acquired or disposed indicator, the price and the resulting beneficial ownership.
Choose the code carefully - P for open market purchase, S for sale, M for exercise, F for tax withholding, A for grant, G for gift - because a wrong code misstates the filing.
Add the Rule 10b5-1 check box and the plan adoption date where the trade was made under a plan.
Have the insider or their attorney-in-fact review the draft, then submit on EDGAR before the end of the second business day after the transaction date and capture the accession number.
Send the filed copy to the insider and post it to the investor website where the company undertakes to do so.
checklist.done: each Form 4 is filed with correct codes and the 10b5-1 box before the end of the second business day, with the accession number recorded.

checklist.step: Run the annual Form 5 sweep and the Item 405 delinquency review
actions: Within 45 days after fiscal year end reconcile each insider's transaction ledger to their filed forms and identify any transaction exempt from Form 4 that must be reported on Form 5, such as certain small acquisitions and gifts.
Obtain a written year-end representation from each insider that all reportable transactions have been reported, or file the Form 5 where they have not.
List every form filed late in the year with the insider name, the transaction and the number of days late.
Draft the Item 405 delinquent reports disclosure for the proxy naming the person, the number of late reports and the transactions involved, and have General Counsel approve it.
checklist.done: the Form 5 sweep is completed within 45 days with insider representations obtained and the Item 405 disclosure drafted from an evidenced late list.

checklist.step: Clear the proxy through the Disclosure Committee and the board committees
actions: Circulate the full draft to the Compensation Committee for the compensation discussion and analysis and the tables, and to the Audit Committee for the audit committee report and the fee table.
Obtain the Compensation Committee's approval of the CD and A and its statement that it reviewed and discussed it with management, which Item 407(e)(5) requires for the compensation committee report.
Resolve every comment before typesetting and record the resolution against the comment.
Have the board approve the meeting notice, the record date and the proxy in a minuted resolution.
checklist.done: both committees have approved their sections with the required reports, comments are resolved on the record, and the board has approved the proxy.

checklist.step: File the definitive proxy and set the notice and access materials live
actions: File the definitive proxy on Schedule 14A on EDGAR no later than the date the materials are first sent to security holders and record the accession number and timestamp.

Confirm the transfer agent posted the proxy and annual report to the notice and access website by the date the notice was sent, and that the notice went out at least 40 calendar days before the meeting.
Confirm the cover page tags and the pay versus performance and other required Inline XBRL tagging validate without error.
Confirm the proxy card matches the matters in the proxy statement exactly, including the say-on-frequency choices where applicable.
checklist.done: the definitive proxy is filed no later than first distribution, materials are posted for the 40-day notice, and tagging and the card are verified.

checklist.step: Incorporate Part III by reference or file the 10-K/A in time
actions: Confirm the 10-K Part III items state that the information is incorporated by reference from the definitive proxy and identify the proxy by its expected filing.
Monitor the 120-day gate: if the definitive proxy will not be filed within 120 days after fiscal year end, prepare a 10-K/A carrying the Part III information in full and file it before day 120.
Confirm each Part III item - Items 10 through 14 - is fully covered by the proxy sections cross-referenced, with no item left uncovered.
Record the decision and the filing on the reporting calendar and in the filing binder.
checklist.done: Part III is covered either by a proxy filed inside 120 days or by a 10-K/A filed before day 120, with item-by-item coverage confirmed.

checklist.step: Report the meeting results on Form 8-K Item 5.07
actions: Obtain the inspector of election's certified report of the vote on each matter with votes for, against, abstentions and broker non-votes.
Prepare the Item 5.07 disclosure listing each matter and its certified tallies, and where a say-on-frequency vote was held, report the frequency the company will adopt.
File on EDGAR within 4 business days of the meeting and record the accession number.
Update the governance calendar with the next say-on-pay and say-on-frequency due years derived from this year's vote.
checklist.done: certified results are filed on Item 5.07 within 4 business days and the next vote due years are diarised.

checklist.step: Archive the proxy and Section 16 file for the retention period
actions: Assemble the file: questionnaires, related person transaction reviews and minutes, compensation table workpapers and tie-out, beneficial ownership tabulation, Schedule 14A checklist, filed proxy and 8-K, and every Section 16 form with its transaction support and power of attorney.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by fiscal year, insider name and accession number.
Confirm the archived proxy is hash-identical to the version accepted by EDGAR.
Run a test retrieval by insider name and confirm the transaction ledger and forms return within one business day.
checklist.done: the proxy and Section 16 file is archived under a 7-year label, hash-matched to EDGAR and retrievable by insider name.

testing.step: Build the population of required governance filings and insider transactions
actions: Pull the registrant's full EDGAR index for the year and isolate the DEF 14A, any PRE 14A, the 10-K and any 10-K/A and the Item 5.07 8-K.
Pull every Form 3, 4 and 5 filed for the registrant's insiders in the year with filing dates and transaction dates.
Build the expected insider transaction population independently from the equity administration system, the designated broker feeds and the payroll withholding records, not from the filed forms.
Reconcile the expected transactions to the filed forms and list every transaction with no matching filing.
testing.done: the expected transaction population is built from source systems and reconciled to the filed forms with unmatched items listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the insider list to the source of record
actions: Agree the Section 16 insider list to the board resolution designating officers and to the director roster on the board portal for every day of the year.
Cross-check against the HRIS for anyone appointed to an executive committee role during the year who was never designated, applying the Rule 16a-1(f) policy-making function test.
Confirm each insider's start and end dates on the list match their appointment and departure dates.
List any person who should have been an insider and was not, since their unreported trades are the highest risk in this population.
testing.done: the insider list ties to the board resolution and the HRIS with any undesignated policy-making officer identified.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of filings, transactions and disclosures
actions: Take 100% of Forms 3 and 5, 100% of transactions by the CEO, CFO and directors, and 100% of related person transactions identified.
Draw 30 further Form 4 transactions at random with a recorded seed, plus 15 compensation table figures and 10 beneficial ownership lines.
Record the population sizes, the seed and the draw date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Confirm the reviewer prepared none of the sampled forms, tables or tabulations.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all Forms 3 and 5 and senior insider trades, and carries no self-review.

testing.step: Reperform the Schedule 14A completeness judgement on sampled items
actions: Read the current text of each sampled Schedule 14A item on eCFR and conclude yourself what the proxy must contain before reading the checklist.
Locate the disclosure in the filed proxy and confirm every element of the item is covered, including the specific dollar thresholds and time periods each item names.
Challenge every not applicable marking by identifying the fact that would make it applicable and testing whether that fact existed.
Confirm the next year's Rule 14a-8 proposal deadline disclosed is exactly 120 calendar days before the anniversary of this year's release date.
testing.done: each sampled item has an independent completeness conclusion read against current rule text, with the 14a-8 date recomputed.

testing.step: Reperform the compensation table and ownership tie-out
actions: Trace each sampled Summary Compensation Table figure to payroll, the equity administration system, the ASC 718 valuation, the incentive scorecard, the actuarial pension calculation or the perquisite log.
Independently re-run the named executive officer determination for the year and confirm the right five people are in the table.
Recompute the CEO pay ratio using the disclosed methodology and confirm the median employee identification is supported by a documented population and measure.
Recompute two beneficial ownership percentages including only that holder's own 60-day exercisable shares in the denominator.
testing.done: sampled compensation figures, the named executive officer set, the pay ratio and sampled ownership percentages are independently recomputed.

testing.step: Recompute Section 16 filing deadlines transaction by transaction
actions: For each sampled Form 4, recompute the deadline as the end of the second business day after the transaction date, excluding weekends and federal holidays, and compare it to the EDGAR acceptance timestamp.
Recompute each Form 3 against the 10-day requirement from the date the person became a director or Section 16 officer, and each Form 5 against 45 days after fiscal year end.
Where a trade was made under a Rule 10b5-1 plan, confirm the box is checked and the plan adoption date given, since an unchecked box misstates the filing.
Record the days late for every breach and compare the resulting list to the Item 405 delinquency disclosure in the proxy.
testing.done: every sampled filing deadline is recomputed against the acceptance timestamp and the late list is compared to the Item 405 disclosure.

testing.step: Trace sampled transactions to broker and equity system evidence
actions: For each sampled transaction obtain the broker confirmation or the equity administration system record showing the date, the share count and the price.
Compare the transaction code on the form to the actual nature of the transaction and treat a wrong code as a misstated filing rather than a typo.
Recompute the resulting beneficial ownership figure on the form by rolling forward the prior filing and confirm it agrees.
Confirm each transaction had a pre-clearance approval on or before the trade date, or log an insider trading policy breach.
testing.done: each sampled transaction traces to broker evidence with the code, the price and the rolled-forward holdings independently verified.

testing.step: Verify the related person transaction search was more than self-reporting
actions: Re-run the name search yourself against the accounts payable and accounts receivable masters using the related person list including immediate family names.
Test any counterparty entity where a related person is an officer, director or holds an equity interest above 10 percent, since Item 404 reaches indirect material interests.
Compare each identified transaction amount to the 120,000 dollar threshold and confirm those above it appear in the filed Item 404 disclosure.
Confirm every disclosed transaction was reviewed under the policy and minuted by the designated committee.
testing.done: an independent ledger search identifies related person transactions, and every one above threshold is disclosed and minuted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the insider or the disclosure item, the filing accession number, the day count where a deadline was missed and whether the filed document is wrong.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list - trade not reported to the company, broker feed gap, wrong transaction code, insider not designated, table figure not tied to source, related person not searched in the ledgers, 120-day Part III gate missed - and an owner.
For every late Section 16 filing confirm the Item 405 disclosure will name it, and for any misstated form require a Form 4/A with General Counsel sign-off.
Set remediation dates before the next trading window opens and carry open issues into the next monthly timeliness test.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with accession number, day count, root cause, owner, remediation date and an amendment or Item 405 decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: State the results against each zero-tolerance criterion - late Forms 3, 4 and 5, the proxy filing versus first distribution date, the 120-day Part III gate and compensation table tie-out differences - each with a count.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective - with the workpaper reference behind each result.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no sampled form, table or tabulation, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and file the signed workpaper against the proxy accession number in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states counts against each criterion and a conclusion, reported to both committees and archived by accession number.
