checklist.step: Define who is in scope for the fitness assessment and keep the roster current
actions: Maintain a roster covering every director, every Section 16 officer designated by board resolution and every officer or director of a licensed insurance subsidiary, since the state requirements reach the subsidiary boards.
Tag each person in the HRIS with their in-scope reason so the screening and notice tasks generate automatically on any appointment.
Reconcile the roster monthly to the board portal director list, the HRIS executive population and the subsidiary annual statement officer pages.
Record start and end dates so the roster shows who was in scope on any given date, not only today.
checklist.done: a dated roster covers parent directors, Section 16 officers and subsidiary officers and reconciles monthly to the board portal, HRIS and annual statements.

checklist.step: Run the background screening before the appointment is effective
actions: Commission the screening package from the approved vendor: criminal record, credit and bankruptcy, civil litigation, regulatory and licensing sanctions, employment and education verification and adverse media, with an international check where the individual has lived abroad.
Obtain the individual's written consent under the Fair Credit Reporting Act before the report is ordered and file the consent.
Set the appointment workflow so the effective date cannot be entered in the HRIS until the screening result is attached.
Where the report shows an adverse item, follow the FCRA pre-adverse action process and give the individual the chance to correct the record before any decision.
checklist.done: no appointment is effective without an attached screening result, a filed consent and a documented adverse-item process where applicable.

checklist.step: Review the ten-year legal proceedings history for Item 401(f)
actions: Apply the Item 401(f) list over the last ten years: bankruptcy of an entity where the person was an executive, criminal convictions other than traffic offences, court or regulatory orders limiting involvement in banking insurance or securities activities, SEC or CFTC findings of securities law violations and any exchange sanction.

Compare the individual's questionnaire answers to the background report and to a direct search of the SEC administrative proceedings, FINRA BrokerCheck and the relevant state insurance department enforcement pages.
Write a memo per person stating each category tested, what was found and whether disclosure is required in the proxy or the 10-K.
Save the memo and the supporting searches in the individual's iManage file.
checklist.done: each in-scope person has a memo testing every Item 401(f) category against independent searches with a disclosure conclusion.

checklist.step: Assess conflicts, outside directorships and time commitment
actions: Review the questionnaire disclosures of other public and private directorships, trusteeships and business interests against the governance guidelines overboarding limit.
Test each outside interest for competitive conflict with the group's insurance operations, for a customer or vendor relationship and for a relationship with the audit firm.

Where the person will serve on the audit committee, confirm the guideline limit on simultaneous audit committee service is met and that the board determines their service does not impair effectiveness.
Record the conclusion and any condition imposed, such as recusal from a category of decisions, and minute it.
checklist.done: each person has a documented conflict, overboarding and audit committee service assessment with any conditions minuted.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the state insurance biographical affidavit
actions: Complete the NAIC Biographical Affidavit for each new officer or director of a licensed insurance subsidiary, covering employment history, ownership interests, litigation and regulatory history, and have it notarised.
Order the independent third-party verification report from the NAIC-authorised vendor and confirm it is dated within the window the state accepts, commonly three years.
Check the state notification matrix for every state of licence and file the change-of-officer or change-of-director notice within the state's deadline, commonly 30 days from the change.
Track each submission to an acknowledgement or non-disapproval and record the file number, and escalate any state that raises an objection to General Counsel the same day.
checklist.done: each subsidiary officer has a notarised affidavit and a current verification report, and every state notice is filed within its deadline and acknowledged.

checklist.step: Approve the appointment and make the securities law filings
actions: Take the fitness pack - screening, legal proceedings memo, conflicts assessment and affidavit status - to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and the board, and minute the appointment.
File the Form 8-K Item 5.02 within 4 business days of the appointment or departure with the required biography and any compensation arrangement.
Open the Section 16 onboarding: obtain EDGAR credentials and a power of attorney and file the Form 3 within 10 days.
Add the person to the insider list, the pre-clearance system and the questionnaire distribution.
checklist.done: the appointment is minuted on a complete fitness pack and the 8-K, Form 3 and insider system onboarding are all completed on time.

checklist.step: Re-assess every in-scope person annually
actions: Issue the annual questionnaire refresh covering new litigation, regulatory matters, directorships, conflicts and family relationships, with the ten-year Item 401(f) look-back restated.
Re-run the sanctions, regulatory and adverse media searches for every in-scope person rather than relying on the appointment-date report.
Compare the answers to the prior year and investigate every change, since the material risk is the item that arose after appointment.
Update the fitness memo with the re-assessment date and conclusion and take any adverse change to the committee.
checklist.done: every in-scope person has a dated annual re-assessment with fresh searches and prior-year differences investigated.

checklist.step: Gate every trading plan through pre-clearance before adoption
actions: Require the individual to submit the draft Rule 10b5-1 plan to the pre-clearance desk before signing, with the broker, the plan type and the intended first trade date.
Confirm the person may only adopt during an open trading window and while not aware of material non-public information.
Confirm the plan contains the required director and officer certification that at adoption they are not aware of material non-public information and are adopting in good faith.
Check for an overlapping plan and for a second single-trade plan within 12 months, both of which lose the affirmative defence, and refuse the plan rather than accepting a condition.
Record the approval, the adoption date and the plan terms in the pre-clearance register.
checklist.done: no plan is adopted without pre-clearance, an open window, the required certification and an overlap and single-trade check on the record.

checklist.step: Compute and enforce the cooling-off period before the first trade
actions: For a director or Section 16 officer compute the cooling-off end date as the later of 90 days after adoption and 2 business days after the disclosure of the financial results for the fiscal quarter in which the plan was adopted, subject to a maximum of 120 days after adoption.
For any other person apply the 30-day cooling-off period.
Write the computed earliest trade date into the plan instruction to the broker and confirm the broker acknowledges it in writing.
Set a monitoring alert so any executed trade before that date is caught the same day and escalated to General Counsel.
checklist.done: each plan carries a computed earliest trade date acknowledged by the broker with same-day monitoring for early execution.

checklist.step: Collect trading arrangement activity every quarter
actions: Ten business days before each periodic report, send every director and Section 16 officer a confirmation request asking whether they adopted, modified or terminated any Rule 10b5-1 plan or other trading arrangement during the quarter, requiring a positive or negative answer from each.
Reconcile the answers to the pre-clearance register, the broker plan confirmations and the Form 4 filings that carry the 10b5-1 check box.
Chase every non-responder personally before the disclosure gate, since a silent director is not a negative confirmation.
Record each arrangement with the person, the role, the action, the date, the duration and the aggregate number of securities.
checklist.done: every director and officer has given a positive or negative confirmation reconciled to the register, brokers and Form 4 check boxes.

checklist.step: Draft the Item 408(a) disclosure for the periodic report
actions: For each arrangement disclose the name and title of the person, the date of adoption, modification or termination, the duration of the plan and the aggregate number of securities to be sold or purchased.
State whether the arrangement is intended to satisfy the Rule 10b5-1(c) affirmative defence or is a non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement, which Item 408(a) distinguishes.
Omit the pricing terms, which Item 408(a) does not require, but include every other material term.
Tag the disclosure in Inline XBRL as required and route the draft to General Counsel and the Disclosure Committee before filing.
checklist.done: each arrangement is disclosed with person, title, dates, duration, share count and the affirmative-defence characterisation, tagged and legally reviewed.

checklist.step: Maintain and file the insider trading policy under Item 408(b)
actions: Review the Insider Trading Policy annually against Rule 10b5-1 as amended and confirm it covers trading by directors, officers and employees and by the company itself in its own securities.
Take amendments to the board for approval and record the approval date in the version history.
File the policy as Exhibit 19 to the 10-K and confirm the Item 408(b) statement in the annual report accurately describes whether policies and procedures have been adopted.
Distribute the current policy to every in-scope person and record their acknowledgement.
checklist.done: a board-approved current policy is filed as Exhibit 19, the Item 408(b) statement matches it, and acknowledgements are recorded.

checklist.step: Handle a disqualifying or adverse finding
actions: On any adverse finding, suspend the appointment or, for a serving individual, convene General Counsel, the HR Business Partner and the committee chair within one business day.
Assess whether the finding requires proxy or 10-K disclosure under Item 401(f), a Form 8-K, a notice to a state insurance department or a notification to the listing exchange.
Record the decision, the reasoning and the individual's response, and where the person remains in role, record the mitigating conditions imposed.
Never close an adverse finding on an oral assurance from the individual.
checklist.done: every adverse finding has a dated decision memo covering disclosure, regulator notice and any conditions imposed.

checklist.step: Close out departures and update every downstream record
actions: On a departure, record the effective date in the HRIS and trigger the 8-K Item 5.02, the state change notice and the removal from the insider list once the final Form 4 obligation has run.
Confirm any outstanding Rule 10b5-1 plan is terminated or transferred to the individual's own broker relationship and record which, since a termination is itself an Item 408(a) reportable event.
Revoke system access, delegated authorities and signing authority and confirm the subsidiary board records are updated.
File the departure documentation in the individual's file and note the date the retention clock starts.
checklist.done: each departure triggers the 8-K, the state notice, insider list removal, plan disposition and authority revocation, all dated.

checklist.step: Archive the individual files and roll the assessment calendar
actions: Assemble each individual's file: consent, background report, questionnaire, legal proceedings memo, conflict assessment, biographical affidavit, state acknowledgements, plan documents and certifications, and quarterly confirmations.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from departure rather than from creation so the record survives while the person serves.
Index by person, role, appointment date and state of licence.
Roll the calendar forward with the annual questionnaire date, the re-screening dates and each quarter's confirmation request date populated.
checklist.done: each individual file is archived under a 7-year post-departure label, indexed by person and state, with next year's assessment dates populated.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope individuals and trading arrangements
actions: Extract from the HRIS every director and Section 16 officer appointed, serving or departing during the period with their effective dates.
Extract from each licensed insurance subsidiary's most recent annual statement the officers and directors listed, to catch subsidiary appointments never routed through the parent process.
Build the trading arrangement population independently from the broker plan confirmations, the Form 4 filings carrying the 10b5-1 check box and the pre-clearance register.
Reconcile the three sources and list every individual or arrangement appearing in one and not the others.
testing.done: the individual and trading arrangement populations are built from independent sources and reconciled with every difference listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the board and regulator records
actions: Agree every appointment and departure to a board or committee minute and to the corresponding Form 8-K Item 5.02.
Agree the Section 16 officer designations to the board resolution and test whether any executive with policy-making function was omitted.
Agree the subsidiary officer lists to the state change notices filed and identify any change never notified.
Document each reconciling item with its reason and flag any individual serving without a completed fitness assessment.
testing.done: every appointment ties to a minute, an 8-K and, for subsidiaries, a state notice, with unassessed individuals flagged.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of individuals and arrangements
actions: Take 100% of appointments and departures in the period, 100% of trading arrangements adopted, modified or terminated and 100% of individuals with any adverse screening finding.
Draw 10 further serving directors and officers at random with a recorded seed for the annual re-assessment test.
Record the population sizes, the seed and the draw date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Confirm the reviewer approved none of the sampled appointments and pre-cleared none of the sampled plans.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all appointments, departures and arrangements, and carries no self-review.

testing.step: Reperform the fitness judgement on each sampled individual
actions: Re-run the sanctions, regulatory, litigation and adverse media searches yourself for each sampled person and reach your own conclusion before reading the fitness memo.
Test each Item 401(f) category independently, including the ten-year look-back for bankruptcies of entities where the person was an executive.
Compare your findings to the questionnaire answers and treat any omission by the individual as a finding about the individual, not only about the process.
Confirm the appointment effective date in the HRIS is on or after the screening completion date.
testing.done: each sampled person has an independently re-run search set, an Item 401(f) conclusion and a verified screening-before-appointment sequence.

testing.step: Trace state insurance notices and affidavits to regulator acknowledgements
actions: For each sampled subsidiary officer, locate the notarised NAIC Biographical Affidavit and confirm the third-party verification report is dated within the accepted window.
Locate the change-of-officer notice filed with each state of licence and record the submission date and the state file or confirmation number.
Confirm no state raised an objection that remains open, and confirm any state requiring prior non-disapproval gave it before the person took office.
List every state of licence with no notice on file as an exception regardless of whether the state has queried it.
testing.done: each sampled subsidiary officer traces to a notarised affidavit, a current verification report and a dated notice per state of licence.

testing.step: Recompute the cooling-off period for every sampled plan
actions: For each director or officer plan recompute 90 days after adoption and 2 business days after the filing date of the 10-Q or 10-K disclosing results for the quarter of adoption, take the later, and cap at 120 days after adoption.
Compare the computed earliest trade date to the first execution shown on the broker statements and the corresponding Form 4 transaction date.
For non-officer plans recompute the 30-day period and test it the same way.
Treat any trade before the computed date as a loss of the affirmative defence and escalate to General Counsel the same day.
testing.done: every sampled plan has an independently recomputed cooling-off date compared to the first actual execution.

testing.step: Test the completeness of the Item 408(a) disclosure against the periodic report
actions: Open the filed 10-Q or 10-K and list every arrangement disclosed under Item 408(a) with its person, dates, duration and share count.
Compare that list to the independently built arrangement population and treat any omission as a disclosure failure.

Confirm each disclosure names the person and title, states the action and date, gives the duration and the aggregate securities, and characterises the arrangement as intended or not intended to satisfy Rule 10b5-1(c).
Confirm the quarterly negative confirmations from every director and officer are on file for the quarter, since a missing confirmation means completeness was never established.
testing.done: the filed Item 408(a) disclosure matches the independent population element by element with all confirmations on file.

testing.step: Verify the insider trading policy exhibit and its Item 408(b) statement
actions: Retrieve Exhibit 19 from the filed 10-K on EDGAR and compare it to the board-approved policy version in the board portal.
Confirm the Item 408(b) statement in the annual report accurately reflects whether policies have been adopted and, if not, why not.
Confirm the policy addresses company transactions in its own securities as well as insider transactions.
Confirm acknowledgements exist for every in-scope person for the current version.
testing.done: the filed Exhibit 19 matches the board-approved version, the Item 408(b) statement is accurate and acknowledgements are complete.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the individual, the appointment or plan, the deadline missed with its day count, and whether a filed disclosure or a regulator submission is wrong.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list - appointment effective before screening, questionnaire answer not verified, subsidiary appointment outside the process, state notice not triggered, plan adopted without certification, arrangement not confirmed at quarter end - and an owner.
For any early trade or omitted disclosure, open a legal assessment with General Counsel covering the affirmative defence and any corrective filing.
Set remediation dates before the next quarter-end confirmation cycle and carry open issues into the next quarterly test.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with individual, day count, root cause, owner, remediation date and a legal assessment where required.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: State the results against each zero-tolerance criterion - appointments before screening, missing state notices, undisclosed arrangements and trades inside cooling-off - each with a count.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective - with the workpaper reference behind each result.
Have the independent reviewer, who approved no sampled appointment and pre-cleared no sampled plan, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and, for trading matters, to the Audit Committee, and file the signed workpaper against the periodic report accession number.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states counts against each criterion and a conclusion, reported to both committees and archived by accession number.

checklist.step: Maintain the governance policy register as the single source of truth
actions: Hold one register listing every board-level policy with its owner, approving body, last approval date, next review date, current version number and the website or intranet location where it is published.
Record for each policy the requirement that drives it - a listing standard, an SEC rule, an insurance regulation or a board decision - so the review has a benchmark.
Add any policy the board or a committee adopts during the year to the register within 5 business days of approval.
Publish the register to the board portal so directors can see at a glance which policies are current and which are due.
checklist.done: the register lists every policy with owner, approving body, driver, version, last approval and next review date and is visible on the board portal.

checklist.step: Build the annual review calendar and map each policy to a meeting
actions: Assign each policy to the committee that must review it - the audit committee for the whistleblower and related person transaction policies, the compensation committee for the clawback policy, the nominating committee for the guidelines and code, and the full board for the ERM policy.
Place each policy on a specific meeting agenda so no policy is reviewed only if time allows.
Load the dates into the register and configure the 60, 30 and 10 day reminders to the owner, the Board Governance Lead and the committee chair.
Circulate the calendar to policy owners with the drafting deadline for each redline.
checklist.done: every policy is assigned to a named committee and a specific meeting date with reminders configured and owners notified.

checklist.step: Refresh the Corporate Governance Guidelines
actions: Test the guidelines against NYSE 303A.09, confirming they address director qualification standards, responsibilities, access to management and independent advisers, director compensation, continuing education, management succession and annual performance evaluation of the board.
Update the director overboarding limit, the retirement or tenure policy and the share ownership guideline against current market practice and proxy adviser expectations.
Redline the changes, obtain General Counsel review and present the redline rather than a clean copy to the committee.
After approval, post the current version to the investor website and confirm the 10-K states that it is available there.
checklist.done: the guidelines are tested against every 303A.09 element, approved from a redline and posted with the 10-K availability statement matching.

checklist.step: Refresh the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics
actions: Test the code against NYSE 303A.10 for conflicts of interest, corporate opportunities, confidentiality, fair dealing, protection of assets, compliance with law and reporting of illegal or unethical behaviour, and against Item 406 for the senior financial officers.
Confirm it states that any waiver for a director or executive officer may be made only by the board or a board committee and must be promptly disclosed.

Bring in the year's ethics case themes - claims handling conduct, agent conduct, gifts and entertainment with brokers, and use of policyholder data - so the code reflects the risks the company actually faces.
After approval, publish the code, run the acknowledgement campaign and update the LMS training content.
checklist.done: the code satisfies both 303A.10 and Item 406, names the waiver authority and disclosure duty, and is republished with training and acknowledgements refreshed.

checklist.step: Review the committee charters against current requirements
actions: Compare each charter to the exchange requirement and to what the committee actually did during the year as shown in the minutes.
Add any new duty the board has taken on - cybersecurity oversight, artificial intelligence governance, climate and sustainability risk - to the charter of the committee that in fact performs it.
Remove duties no longer performed rather than leaving a charter that overstates the committee's work.
Present the redline to the committee, obtain its recommendation and take it to the board for approval.
checklist.done: each charter matches both the exchange requirement and the committee's actual practice, approved from a redline by the board.

checklist.step: Review and evidence the Compensation Recovery clawback policy
actions: Confirm the policy meets the listing standard adopted under Rule 10D-1: recovery of erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation received by current and former executive officers in the three completed fiscal years preceding the date a restatement is required, on a no-fault basis.
Confirm it covers both a Big R and a little r restatement and that recovery is mandatory with only the narrow impracticability exceptions.
Test the policy against the year's incentive plans to confirm every incentive-based award is captured, including plans at insurance subsidiaries.
Confirm the policy is filed as Exhibit 97 to the 10-K and that the cover page check boxes on restatement and recovery analysis are answered correctly.
checklist.done: the clawback policy meets the Rule 10D-1 listing standard, covers all incentive plans, and is filed as Exhibit 97 with the cover page boxes verified.

checklist.step: Review the cybersecurity governance the board actually performs
actions: Confirm the information security policy names the board committee with cybersecurity oversight, the reporting cadence to it and the management position responsible, since Item 106(c) requires all three to be described.
Present to that committee at the agreed cadence covering the risk assessment results, third-party and vendor risk, incident metrics, penetration test findings and remediation status.

Confirm the incident response procedure includes the materiality determination step that starts the 4-business-day Form 8-K Item 1.05 clock, and that Legal and the Disclosure Committee are named participants.
Record the directors' relevant expertise and the training given so the Item 106(c) description is supportable.
checklist.done: the policy names the overseeing committee, the cadence and the responsible management position, and the actual reporting and incident escalation match.

checklist.step: Review the risk appetite and enterprise risk management policy
actions: Present the refreshed risk appetite statement with the quantitative limits for underwriting, reserving, credit, market, liquidity, operational and cyber risk to the board risk committee.
Reconcile the appetite limits to the ORSA summary report filed with the lead state insurance regulator so the group tells the same story to the board and the regulator.
Report actual position against each limit for the year with breaches, their causes and the actions taken.
Obtain the board's approval of the appetite and record the resolution with the limits attached rather than referenced.
checklist.done: the board approves a risk appetite with quantitative limits reconciled to the ORSA and a year of actual-versus-limit reporting attached.

checklist.step: Prepare the board pack so approval is informed rather than nominal
actions: For each policy prepare a one-page summary stating what changed, why, what requirement drives it, what the alternatives were and what management recommends.
Attach the redline against the approved version and the legal review note confirming the policy meets its driving requirement.
Load the pack to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting so directors have reading time.
Track which directors opened the materials and follow up with anyone who has not before the meeting.
checklist.done: each policy reaches the board with a change summary, a redline and a legal review note, distributed at least 5 business days ahead.

checklist.step: Obtain and record the approval resolution
actions: Draft the resolution naming the policy, the version number and the effective date rather than approving an unversioned document.
Minute the discussion, the questions asked, any amendment made in the meeting and the vote, including any abstention.
Where the meeting amends the policy, reissue the final version incorporating the amendment and have the chair confirm it matches the resolution.
Update the register with the approval date, the new version number and the next review date within 5 business days.
checklist.done: each approval is a versioned, dated resolution with the minuted discussion and the register updated within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Publish the approved versions and retire the superseded ones
actions: Publish the approved version to the investor website for the externally required policies and to the intranet policy library for all of them, on the effective date.
Remove or archive the superseded version so no one can retrieve it as current, and keep it in the version history for the retention period.
Confirm every link in the 10-K, the proxy and the intranet resolves to the current version.
Notify affected functions - Claims, Underwriting, Distribution, Finance and IT - of the changes and what they must do differently.
checklist.done: approved versions are live on the effective date, superseded versions are unreachable as current, every disclosed link resolves and functions are notified.

checklist.step: Run acknowledgement and training on the changed policies
actions: Assign acknowledgement of each materially changed policy to the affected population in the learning management system with a completion deadline.
Update the training content where the change alters what an employee must do, rather than only circulating the document.
Reconcile the assignment list to the HRIS active headcount and the board portal director list, and chase non-completers weekly.
Report completion rates to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee with the names of any officer or director outstanding.
checklist.done: acknowledgement and training are assigned and reconciled to headcount, with completion reported and outstanding officers named.

checklist.step: Feed the policy record into the Item 407 and Item 106 disclosures
actions: Draft the Item 407(h) board leadership structure and risk oversight disclosure describing the actual committee allocation of risk oversight and why the leadership structure is appropriate.

Draft the Item 106(c) cybersecurity governance disclosure naming the overseeing committee, the reporting cadence and the responsible management position, drawn from the minutes rather than from the policy text.
Confirm the availability statements for the guidelines and the code give working URLs, and confirm Exhibits 19 and 97 are attached to the 10-K.
Route the package to General Counsel and the Disclosure Committee before typesetting.
checklist.done: the Item 407(h) and Item 106(c) disclosures are drafted from the minutes, the URLs resolve and Exhibits 19 and 97 are attached.

checklist.step: Manage overdue policies and policy exceptions
actions: Run the governance dashboard monthly and list every policy past its review date with the owner and the days overdue.
Escalate anything over 30 days overdue to the committee chair and require a dated recovery plan.
For any exception granted to a policy, record the requester, the risk accepted, the compensating control, the approving executive and an expiry date no longer than one review cycle.
Report the overdue and exception position to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee at each meeting.
checklist.done: overdue policies and live exceptions are reported monthly with owners, days overdue, risk accepted and expiry dates.

checklist.step: Archive the policy year and roll the cycle forward
actions: Archive each approved version with its redline, board pack summary, legal review note, resolution, minute extract and publication confirmation.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by policy name, version number and approval date.
Confirm the archived version is hash-identical to the version published and, where applicable, to the exhibit filed on EDGAR.
Roll the register forward with next year's review dates and confirm the reminders are armed.
checklist.done: each policy version is archived with its full approval trail under a 7-year label, hash-matched to the published and filed versions, with next year's dates armed.

testing.step: Build the population of policies requiring board or committee approval
actions: Export the governance policy register with owner, approving body, last approval date, version and next review date.
Independently rebuild the expected list from the exchange listing standards, the SEC rules requiring a policy or an exhibit, and the insurance regulatory expectations for the group.
List any policy required by a rule but absent from the register - a missing policy is a worse finding than a late one.
Reconcile the register to the intranet policy library and the investor website and list any published policy that is not on the register.
testing.done: the register is reconciled to an independently rebuilt requirement list, the intranet and the website, with missing policies identified.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the minutes as the source of record
actions: For every approval date shown on the register, locate the board or committee minute and confirm the resolution names the policy and the version approved.
Confirm the approving body matches the one the register assigns, since approval by the wrong committee does not satisfy the requirement.
Confirm no policy shows an approval date with no corresponding minute and no minute approves a policy absent from the register.
Document each reconciling item with its explanation.
testing.done: every register approval date traces to a minuted, versioned resolution by the correct body, with differences explained.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of policies for detailed testing
actions: Take 100% of the policies filed as exhibits or referenced in the 10-K and proxy - the code, the guidelines, the insider trading policy and the clawback policy - and 100% of policies amended in the year.
Draw 8 further policies at random with a recorded seed from the remaining register.
Record the population size, the seed and the draw date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Confirm the reviewer owns none of the sampled policies.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all disclosed and amended policies, and carries no self-review.

testing.step: Reperform the content sufficiency judgement on the sampled policies
actions: Read the current text of the driving requirement - NYSE 303A.09 or 303A.10, Item 406, Rule 10D-1 or Item 106 - and list what the policy must contain before reading the policy.
Test the approved policy text against that list element by element and cite the section satisfying each element.
Challenge any element the company treats as covered by practice rather than by the policy text.
Treat a policy that meets the letter but describes a practice the company does not follow as a substantive exception, not a drafting point.
testing.done: each sampled policy is tested element by element against the current requirement text with section citations and practice alignment checked.

testing.step: Compare the published, filed and board-approved versions
actions: Download each sampled policy from the investor website and the intranet and compare it to the board-approved version in the archive using a text comparison, not a visual check.
For the insider trading policy and the clawback policy, download Exhibits 19 and 97 from the filed 10-K on EDGAR and compare them the same way.
Confirm version numbers and effective dates match across all copies.
Treat any difference as a fail regardless of whether it changes the meaning, because shareholders were given a document the board did not approve.
testing.done: published, filed and board-approved versions are text-compared and match on content, version number and effective date.

testing.step: Recompute the review cadence and overdue ageing
actions: For every policy on the register recompute the months elapsed from the last approval date to the test date and list anything over 12 months.
Recompute the next review dates and confirm they fall inside the cadence the register states rather than being pushed to suit meeting agendas.
For each policy amended in the year, recompute the days from board approval to publication and to the update of the register.
Compare the overdue list you compute to the overdue list reported to the committee and treat any under-reporting as a separate exception.
testing.done: review ageing, next-review dates and publication lags are independently recomputed and compared to what the committee was told.

testing.step: Trace the Item 106 and Item 407(h) disclosures to actual board activity
actions: Read the filed Item 106(c) disclosure and identify the committee, the cadence and the management position it names.
Locate in the minutes each cybersecurity report to that committee in the year and confirm the actual cadence matches the disclosed cadence.
Read the Item 407(h) risk oversight disclosure and trace each stated allocation of risk oversight to a charter provision and to minuted activity.
Treat a disclosure describing a cadence or an allocation the minutes do not support as a disclosure exception for General Counsel.
testing.done: the disclosed cybersecurity cadence and risk oversight allocation are each traced to charter provisions and dated minutes.

testing.step: Test acknowledgement and exception records behind the sampled policies
actions: For each materially amended sampled policy, pull the acknowledgement completion report and reconcile the assignment population to HRIS headcount and the director roster.
Confirm every officer and director completed acknowledgement and identify any outstanding by name.
Pull every live exception to a sampled policy and confirm each has an approver, a compensating control, an accepted risk and an expiry date inside one review cycle.
List any exception that has been renewed more than once without a committee decision.
testing.done: acknowledgement populations reconcile to headcount and every live exception has an approver, a control, a risk and an unexpired date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the policy, its version, the requirement implicated and whether a published or filed document is wrong.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list - policy missing from the register, review slipped past 12 months, approved by the wrong body, published version not the approved version, exhibit not refiled after amendment, disclosure not supported by minutes - and an owner.
For any published or filed version mismatch, require republication or an exhibit refiling with General Counsel sign-off.
Set remediation dates before the next committee meeting and carry open issues into the next annual policy test.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with the policy version, root cause, owner, remediation date and a republication decision where needed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the board committee
actions: State the results against each zero-tolerance criterion - policies over 12 months without approval, version mismatches between approved, published and filed copies, and missing exhibits - each with a count.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective - with the workpaper reference behind each result.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns none of the sampled policies, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and to the Audit Committee for the disclosure findings, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states counts against each criterion and a conclusion, reported to both committees and archived.
